title: De-share `InitContainer` type from `Container`
body:
In order to simplify future KEPs and allow more flexibility on adding new fields and behaviors on Containers I suggest we fork the type of `InitContainer` and regular `Container`.

This de-sharing will be very helpful with the Sidecar containers KEP https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/3759 where we want to introduce a new field on Init containers, but not on any other containers.

There will be more requests for change of these types going forward and de-sharing of types will simplify discussions and improve velocity of features development.

It will also allow us to have a better documentation of Init Containers type - today the same documentation for each field is used. 

## Existing approach

We already have a precedence in code where `EphemeralContainer` is a separate type from `Container`. The way it's implemented is by introducing a collection `EphemeralContainerCommon` that contains all the same fields as a regular `Container` so it can be casted to the `Container` type. See the [type definition](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5a2dd64801f0f9887047b6d0f618d88532d4a32d/pkg/apis/core/types.go#L3462-L3477) and a [test](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1f02f43ec6910cbcd46222b16a2f3965458e5e45/pkg/apis/core/types_test.go#L24-L41).

This approach simplified the development in some places, but made types heavily interdependent so no new fields can be added to the `Container` type without updating `EphemeralContainer` as well.

## Proposed

The proposal is to completely split these types making them a separate types that cannot be casted to one another.

This will require some changes in interfaces, mostly for the various resource managers. Those interfaces will be extended to provide separate API methods for `InitContainer` and a regular `Container`.

There are a few places that may need to iterate over all containers making similar changes. If those patterns common across the code, we will implement helpe

title: windows kube-proxy: "externalTrafficPolicy: Local" results in no clusterIP entry in windows node
body:
I am tracking a changed behavior in networking with kubernetes 1.26. If I create a service of type externalTrafficPolicy: Local, and there are no local endpoints in a node, kube-proxy does not create hns loadbalancers for the clusterIP of that service. 

With kubernetes 1.25, it creates a loadbalancer for clusterIP (but not externalIP). 

This is the relevant log message:
```
"Skipped creating Hns LoadBalancer for cluster ip resources. Reason : all endpoints are terminating" clusterIP="10.114.142.98" nodeport=31336 allEndpointsTerminating=true 
```

Looks like this comes with a result from a new function isAllEndpointsTerminating introduced in kubernetes 1.26.

In Linux, we can still access clusterIP even if there are no local endpoints for the service. Thoughts?

The end result is that in Windows, clients cannot access the clusterIP of such a service with there are no local endpoints.

title: Investigate callers of IsLikelyNotMountPoint
body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!-->


**What happened**:
IsLikelyNotMountPoint() doesn't detect bind mounts of directories on the same fs as /var/lib/kubelet.  Local PVs that are directories on the rootfs are most problematic.  Similar CSI plugins that expose rootfs directories are also problematic. 

[This commit](https://github.com/msau42/kubernetes/commit/559fdd5229eb550054df57d1854d58dc4cd7c506) identifies some functions that are technically incorrect because they use IsLikelyNotMountPoint() instead of IsNotMountPoint().  However, IsNotMountPoint() is expensive since it has to scan all mount points on the host, so instead of changing the callers to use IsNotMountPoint(), we found other ways to fix the problem.

We should investigate all other uses of IsLikelyNotMountPoint() to see if these cases are handled.

 The back-off limit is set by default to 6. Failed Pods associated with the Job are recreated by the Job controller with an exponential back-off delay (10s, 20s, 40s ...) capped at six minutes.

title: Update storage e2e test suite running in Windows to add a nodeSelector for Window nodes
body:
### What would you like to be added?

The current process to test a CSI driver in Windows nodepools is:

- Create a cluster with a Windows nodepool, by default the Window nodes are tainted with `NoSchedule`
- Install a CSI Driver, assume it has a node component that can run in Windows
- Untaint the Windows nodes and *taint the Linux nodes*
- Run the e2e tests

We taint the Linux nodes because the code to deploy the test pods (the ones with the agnhost image) don't use a node selector, this issue is about identifying that the tests are supposed to run in Windows with the `--node-distro` flag, based on that we can add the `kubernetes.io/os=windows` node selector to the test pods, probably we'd also need to add a toleration to the pods so that they can be scheduled without removing the taint, although removing it should be ok too.
 
/sig storage
cc @mattcary @msau42 

### Why is this needed?

We'd like to run the e2e tests without making changes to the taints set on the nodes.

title: kube-apiserver: some HTTP requests might hang indefinitely
body:
### What happened?

Since `kube-apiserver` doesn't specify a `WriteTimeout` on the server level it solely relies on the timeout filter to terminate HTTP requests.

The timeout filter wraps the `http.ResponseWriter` into a time-aware construct and passes it to an HTTP handler. Once the specified timeout has elapsed the HTTP handler loses control and an appropriate response is sent back to a client.

The issue arises when a response written via the `http.ResponseWriter.Write` method cannot be sent to the client. In that scenario, the timeout handler won't be able to terminate the connection because it cannot acquire a lock and the HTTP request will hang forever.

The `Write` method does not always send immediately data to the client. Most of the time anything sent via the `Write` method is actually stored in a memory buffer and sent to the client at a later time. It only sends data immediately when the buffer is sufficiently large.

Now, with the introduction of `HTTP2/ping` feature, stale connections are detected and terminated. But what if the connection isn't stale but the client is still slow to download data? Exactly in those cases, the `kube-apiserver` won't be able to terminate hanging HTTP requests.

### What did you expect to happen?

the `kube-apiserver` should always terminate timed-out HTTP requests.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. update the `OpenAPI` spec so that it exceeds the HTTP buffer.
2. send an HTTP request for that spec but don't actually download it. (not closing the `ResponseBody` does the trick). For example:
```
req, _ := http.NewRequest("GET", `/openapi/v2`, nil)
resp, _ := rt.RoundTrip(req)
// don't close the rsp body, usually you would: resp.Body.Close()
// sleep for 1 hour
```

title: In-place rolling updates
body:
Our current rolling update scheme requires deleting a pod and creating a replacement. We should also have rolling "in-place" update, of both containers and pods. There are two kinds of in-place update
1) [only applies to container update] pod stays in place, but container doesn't - for example, change container image without killing pod
2) [applies to pod or container update] pod stays in place, and container stays in place - for example, resource limit updates (IIRC we don't implement this yet, or at least don't implement it in-place)

The motivation is that there's no reason to kill the pod if you don't need to. The user may have local data stored in it that they don't want blown away due to update.

[E2E] Support for pulling images from private registry
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Our team is using sonobuoy to run the conformance tests on a cluster. When running Sonobuoy E2E/Conformance tests, deployed pods will go into an ErrImagePull/ImagePullBackOff state when the image resides in a repository that requires authentication, and credentials are not passed with the request.

The [E2E/Conformance test](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/test/e2e) process spawns pods in separate namespaces to run E2E/Conformance tests. If pods are referencing images from a private registry, the secrets wouldn’t be available in the newly created namespaces and the pod will fail to start.

This is the issue reported by one of the sonobuoy users - https://github.com/vmware-tanzu/sonobuoy/issues/1038

Kubernetes E2E framework provides a `--e2e-docker-config-file`  flag which takes in a file containing the credentials that can be used to pull images from private registries needed for a test.  Using the credentials a secret can be created in the newly created namespace. 
With the Secret created, the default service account (in the new namespace) will be patched with the created secret and can then be referenced by the test pod, and repository authentication should be successful.


### Why is this needed?

As of now, when running the E2E tests, the flag is only being checked in a single test - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/57eb5d631ccd615cd161b6da36afc759af004b93/test/e2e/common/node/runtime.go#L292-L308
so despite passing the credential file, other tests would fail.

title: Topology Spread Constraints does not respect taints
body:
### What happened?

Created a kind cluster with one control plane node and three worker nodes. Created a deployment with 7 replicas and  topology constraint with key `kubernetes.io/hostname` and `maxSkew` set to 1. Only three pods got scheduled; others are in pending state.

### What did you expect to happen?

All seven pods get scheduled in three worker nodes with a distribution of (2,2,3). 

The filter takes the control plane node into account. The control plane node has a taint and no pods (except the one having toleration) can be scheduled there. For three pods, the distribution is (0,1,1,1) where the first element represents the control plane node. Scheduling any more pods is not possible; adding to control plane node is not possible because of the taint; adding to any of the worker nodes is not possible as it will violate the topology spread constraints.

It's understandable that the plugin works as expected. But, it's good to incorporate the intelligence of ignoring the tainted nodes.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

### config.yaml

```
kind: Cluster
apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4
nodes:
- role: control-plane
- role: worker

title: Decoding should not clear apiVersion/kind
body:
**What would you like to be added**:
When using a typed client, decoding to a versioned struct (not an internal API type), the apiVersion/kind information returned from the server should not be dropped.

**Why is this needed**:
The `GroupVersionKind()` method included in the ObjectKind interface is largely useless when dealing with arbitrary runtime.Object instances, since typed instances drop this information here:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/69a34f6a6f67de47cb9b72b6ac98e089d301beb3/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/runtime/helper.go#L245-L259

This is the decoder used when a client requests a decoder that does not do conversion:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/69a34f6a6f67de47cb9b72b6ac98e089d301beb3/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/runtime/serializer/codec_factory.go#L175-L179

I could see clearing group/version/kind information when converting to an internal version, but I don't see the benefit of stripping it on decode if we're only dealing with a versioned struct.

/sig api-machinery
/cc @smarterclayton 

Note that https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/3030 still needs to be resolved before apiVersion/kind could be depended on for individual objects for all API responses, but this would at least solve the issue with an update of an object clearing the apiVersion/kind in an update response (xref https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/controller-runtime/issues/526)

title: Admission Controller Webhook configuration rule cannot exclude specific resources
body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:
The webhook configuration (for both `ValidatingWebhookConfiguration` and `MutatingAdmissionWebhook`, reference https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/extensible-admission-controllers/) support `rules` to select what types of resources should be sent to the webhook endpoint. The rule definitions can have a set of `resources` which specifies which resource types should be selected.

What is missing is the ability to specify what resources to exclude. There does not appear to be a way to give any negative selection criteria.

**Why is this needed**:
In practice, systems where an external policy engine like OPA are being used as the webhook endpoint, it is common to want broad coverage of the admission policy. This is typically done by specifying wildcards in the webhook configuration and allowing the policies in OPA to self select what types of objects they apply to.

In these same systems, with wildcard webhook configurations, if the `failurePolicy` is set to `Fail` it is extremely difficult for the `rules` definitions to allow for a cluster to recover in network failure modes.

For example, if for sake of argument, the network is based on Calico and requires objects in the cluster to be modified (eg ippools, felixconfigurations, clusterinformations, bgpconfigurations, bgppeers, etc) when the network is down, the api-server may not be able to successfully call the webhook, which can prevent the network controllers from converging back to a working state. The only way to correct the issue is to remove the webhook, allow the network to repair, and re-apply it. Throughout this time however it means that the cluster is potentially un-protected.

Ideally a cluster admin could configure the webhook to exclude certain resources. The only option right now appears to be to specify *every* type of resource expected to be in the cluster

title: Update go-jose version
body:
### What would you like to be added?

The go-jose dependency version should be updated from v2.2.2 to v2.6.0.

### Why is this needed?

This is to make the kubernetes code compatible with newer go-jose v2 versions that have a small breaking change: `jwt.NewNumericDate()` returns a pointer in newer versions which breaks the kubernetes code [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.0-alpha.2/pkg/serviceaccount/claims.go#L93):
```
/go/pkg/mod/github.com/k3s-io/kubernetes@v1.26.0-k3s1/pkg/serviceaccount/claims.go:93:29: cannot use jwt.NewNumericDate(now.Add(time.Duration(warnafter) * time.Second)) (value of type *jwt.NumericDate) as type jwt.NumericDate in assignment
```
For instance this prevents using the kubernetes apiserver and [ory/fosite](https://github.com/ory/fosite/tree/v0.44.0) together within the same Go codebase.

title: Mount points not propagated as expected when using subpath.
body:
### What happened?

We performed mount in shared emptyDir volume subpath in one container, and read the data through the same mounted subpath in another container. And the container failed to read the data under the mount point occasionally. 

After some investigation, I thought this may be caused by the bind options used during the kubelet preparation the subpath. It use `bind` instead  of `rbind`, and if the mount procedure happens before the subpath bind operation, the sub mounts inside the emptyDir won't be picked up by the new subpath.

### What did you expect to happen?

The mount points should be consistent in each container.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  initContainers:
  - image: ubuntu
    command:
    - bash
    args:
    - "-c"
    - "set -x; touch /data/test_data.txt; mkdir /volume-subpath/mount-point/; mount --bind /data/ /volume-subpath/mount-point/; ls /volume-subpath/mount-point/"
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    name: init
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
    volumeMounts:
    - mountPath: /volume-subpath/
      name: volume
      subPath: sub-path-on-volume/
      mountPropagation: Bidirectional
    - mountPath: /data/
      name: mock-data-entry
  containers:
  - image: ubuntu
    command:
    - bash
    args:
    - "-c"
    - "set -x; ls /volume-subpath/; ls /volume-subpath/mount-point/"
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    name: main-container
    volumeMounts:
    - mountPath: /volume-subpath/
      name: volume
      subPath: sub-path-on-volume/
      mountPropagation: HostToContainer
  restartPolicy: Always
  volumes:
  - name: volume
    emptyDir: {}
  - name: mock-data-entry
    emptyDir: {}
```

Apply this yaml, and the mount created in the init container won't be accessible by the main-container.

title: Inform users about unsupported PDB options
body:
### What happened?

When using PDBs with `MaxUnavailable` or `MinAvailable` (percentage), it is not supported to reference pods via a PDB selector, that do not have a supported controller owner reference:
- Deployment, ReplicationController, ReplicaSet, and StatefulSet controllers
- or a resource implementing `/scale` subresource

This is also documented https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/run-application/configure-pdb/#arbitrary-controllers-and-selectors 

Nevertheless, there are still people who create PDBs a pods without controllers  that ignore this. For example PDBs that set `MaxUnavailable: 0`, want to block eviction, and node drain (it works for them but the PDB status is invalid).

Unfortunately there is no feedback for the user to receive when this happens. The KCM logs is the only place that informs the user when unmanaged pods are found.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f58f70bd5730658505042cd9baa80f72d3b6e31e/pkg/controller/disruption/disruption.go#L709

Which I think is insufficient.  

### What did you expect to happen?

title: PVC recreation needed when Stateful set Pod stuck in pending
body:
### What happened?

- User cordons a node with a pvc bound to a local persistent volume
- User deletes a stateful set pod from that node
- The pod is in pending because the pvc is still bound to a local pv on the cordoned node (expected)
- The node dies and the pvc is deleted
- The pod is still stuck in pending because the pvc is missing (bug)

The pod now needs to be manually deleted so that the pod+pvc can be recreated

### What did you expect to happen?

After the pvc was deleted, the statefulset controller should have recreated it and bound it to a new node's local pv so that the pending pod could be scheduled. Currently the only way to get the pod out of pending is to manually delete it so that it recreates itself and its pvc

We used https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/sig-storage-local-static-provisioner for the local PVs, but the problem is not limited to this particular provisioner

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- create a stateful set with a pvc that is bound to a local PV
- use `kubectl cordon` to cordon a node with a local pv
- delete a statefulset pod from that node
- delete the pvc from that node

the pod is now stuck in pending due to a missing pvc

### Anything else we need to know?

There was a related issue https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/74374 but this only fixed the issue when the order of operations was delete pvc -> delete pod. but in this case, it is delete pod -> delete pvc

title: Inform users about unsupported PDB options
body:
### What happened?

When using PDBs with `MaxUnavailable` or `MinAvailable` (percentage), it is not supported to reference pods via a PDB selector, that do not have a supported controller owner reference:
- Deployment, ReplicationController, ReplicaSet, and StatefulSet controllers
- or a resource implementing `/scale` subresource

This is also documented https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/run-application/configure-pdb/#arbitrary-controllers-and-selectors 

Nevertheless, there are still people who create PDBs a pods without controllers  that ignore this. For example PDBs that set `MaxUnavailable: 0`, want to block eviction, and node drain (it works for them but the PDB status is invalid).

Unfortunately there is no feedback for the user to receive when this happens. The KCM logs is the only place that informs the user when unmanaged pods are found.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f58f70bd5730658505042cd9baa80f72d3b6e31e/pkg/controller/disruption/disruption.go#L709

Which I think is insufficient.  

### What did you expect to happen?

There should be some way to inform users about this. Since it cannot be know on admission we probably have to do it when reconciling the PDB and unmanaged pods are found. Options:

1. create an event when this is detected - probably needs to be throttled in some way
2. manage a condition in a PDB status that would be set and admins could monitor these to detect misbehaving PDBs   

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

create a PDB

```yaml
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: nginx-test

  maxUnavailable: 1

title: Default storage class needs to be present before PVCs are created
body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:

When the PVC is created before the default storage class, PVC will end up in a state with no storage class and will never be bounded to a PV.

#### What you expected to happen:

I expect that in eventually consistent model of Kubernetes, non-bound PVCs with no storage class will get assigned the default class once one is available and get bounded to a PV.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

Create a PVC with no storage class, and then create a StorageClass marked as default.

#### Anything else we need to know?:

The setter of the default storage class on PVCs is currently implemented only as an admission webhook, creating the requirements for the default StorageClass to exist before any PVCs are created. I think similar logic should be executed in PV controller to add the default storage class if PVC is not bound and doesn't have a storage class.

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.19.4

title: Indexed Jobs with high completion counts kill kubelet's performance
body:
### What happened?

An indexed job with 6,000 completions and a parallelism of 20 was run. The majority of those pods landed on a single node. Since kubelet watches all pods that belong to the node, it had to keep those 6,000 pods in memory and loop through them in its control loops. This makes it take unreasonably long for new pods to start up on the node, and causes other node scalability issues.

### What did you expect to happen?

I expect Indexed Jobs to scale one way or another. There seems to be a lot of room for improvement here though.

For starters, I don't think that indexed jobs need to keep pods around in the API for state tracking since the status field of indexed jobs records the completed indexes. If indexed jobs cleaned up pods while actively running, they could scale to infinite numbers of completions without straining the kube API or kubelet.

Additionally, I'd expect kubelet to be able to handle large numbers of Completed pods gracefully. As I understand it, kubelet keeps an eye on completed pods to enable you to do `kubectl logs`, etc to debug why the pod succeeded or failed. In an ideal world, kubelet might have a setting for the maximum number of completed pods to leave on disk (similar to the old max dead containers per pod type settings). With a setting like this, it could leave the pods in the API for the job's state tracking, but stop doing any work on them. Alternatively, maybe a separate control loop could deal with completed pods so that the main kubelet control loop doesn't slow down.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create an Indexed Job with:
- A container that just runs something like `/bin/true`
- A selector that ties its pods to a single node
- A high number of completions (like 6,000 for example)

After a while, you will notice kubelet slowing to a crawl.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

title: If kubelet is unavailable, AttachDetachController fails to force detach on pod deletion
body:
/kind bug

**What you expected to happen**:
When a pod using an attached volume is deleted (gracefully) but kubelet in the corresponding node is down, the AttachDetachController should assume the node is unrecoverable after a timeout (currently 6min) and forcefully detach the volume. 

**What happened**:
The volume is never detached.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
* Create a pod with a volume using any of the attachable plugins (I used GCE PD to test).
* Stop kubelet inside the node where the pod is scheduled.
* Delete the pod.
* Wait for 6min+
* Check to see if the volume is still attached.

**Anything else we need to know?**:
This doesn't happen if the pod is force-deleted.

It's likely due to the last condition checked in [this line](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5e9a5659b751bd1d765758548273198fe8e40642/pkg/volume/util/util.go#L649). Once kubelet is down, the container  status is no longer reported correctly. Inside the Attach Detach Controller, This function is called by the pod update informer handler, which sets whether the volume should be attached in the desired state of the world. On pod force deletion, the pod object is deleted immediately, and this triggers the pod delete informer handler, which doesn't call this function.

/sig storage

title: [Evented PLEG] Kubelet to handle containerEventsResponseCh with nil PodSandboxStatus
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Currently kubelet will panic with nil pointer if podSandboxStatus is nil: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/86284d42f891cac285c08c8a350ca8724f12c21f/pkg/kubelet/pleg/evented.go#L207

For containerd, it is possible that a podSandbox cannot be found when cri tries to stop/remove a container. This could happen when 
1. a pod sandbox (s1) is being created but not yet finished,
2. a container (c1) is being created under the pod sandbox s1.
3. s1 is deleted. Note that since step 2 has not finished yet, it is possible that RemovePodSandbox did not remove the c1.
4. c1 is created. 
5. kubelet requests to delete c1. Since now s1 is deleted, containerd cannot find the sandbox for `c1.SandboxID`. 

Creating this issue to investigate and figure out how kubelet should handle containerEventsResponseCh with nil PodSandboxStatus.



### Why is this needed?

kubelet, with evented PLEG enabled, should be able to handle containerEventsResponseCh with nil PodSandboxStatus

title: scheduler: `ImageLocality` seems to ignore image pull progress
body:
### What happened?

It seems like the scheduler considers two nodes to have the same score even when one node has the image fully pulled and the other has only just begun to pull the image, resulting in long pod startup times, especially for slow-pulling images. I can't 100% tell if the issue is with the ImageLocality plugin, because I'm not sure how to get scoring information (I tried `--v=10`, but it seems like score logging is pending https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/91633). The relevant source code seems to be [here](https://github.com/chendave/kubernetes/blob/46f3e4dfdd4df2d538163d218a0921e8980156b4/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/imagelocality/image_locality.go#L100-L102).

### What did you expect to happen?

All else equal, the scheduler should prefer nodes that have the image completely pulled.

1. Configure scheduler to only care about ImageLocality

title: Discussion on refactoring kubelet to allow writing of integration tests
body:
The pros of integration tests, compared with e2e node tests:
- shorter development cycle
- easier to run the tests from IDE with debugger
- possibility of using a fake clock to make some of the tests faster

However, currently, there is only a single integration test for kubelet, but is very specific: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/integration/kubelet/watch_manager_test.go.

It seems the main reason is that it would require refactoring of kubelet to be able to easily mock its dependencies without access to private fields as unit tests have. 

Not sure what the gain to effort ratio is.

Opening the issue to give it for discussion.

Refactor [`computePodResourceRequest`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/108c284a330a82ce1a1f80238e4f54bf5e8b045a/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/noderesources/fit.go#L162:6) and [`calculateResource`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/108c284a330a82ce1a1f80238e4f54bf5e8b045a/pkg/scheduler/framework/types.go#L715) so that the shared bits can be put in k8s.io/component-helper.

### Why is this needed?

These 2 implementations have the risk of becoming out of sync. Two components depend on it: kube-scheduler and kubelet, so it qualifies for being in the component-helper repo.

I think the major complication is what to do with one of the dependencies of these calculations: [`IsScalarResourceName`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/108c284a330a82ce1a1f80238e4f54bf5e8b045a/pkg/scheduler/util/utils.go#L145), which depend on `k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/apis/core/v1/helper`. We need to evaluate if such check is actually necessary (that is, if removing it would change behavior). I have the suspicion that it wouldn't, assuming an apiserver already validated the Pod on admission.

title: Static pod resources are double counted in kubelet admission because mirror pods are not excluded
body:
### What happened?

When a new pod is admitted to the Kubelet, it is compared to all other "active" pods.  Active pods are the set of pods that have been observed from a config set, minus those that have already failed admission or are in a terminal phase (as the Kubelet sees it).  This check is performed by `Kubelet.GetActivePods()` and calls `kl.filterOutInactivePods()` on the contents of podManager.

During review of #113145 I was reminded that pod manager contains three sets of pods:

* Pods created via the API that are desired to run on this node (API pods)
* Pods created via local config sources that are desired to run on this node (static pods)
* Pods created on the API by the Kubelet to represent static pods (mirror pods)

For every static pod there should be one mirror pod in the API, but sometimes they lag (if the API is down or slow).  Mirror pods are not source of truth - if a Kubelet sees a mirror pod coming from the API it will take no action on it.  So today when we calculate the resources in use on a Kubelet in admission we are double counting the contribution from a single static pod if the mirror pod already exists (such as when a Kubelet is restarted).

This doesn't impact *new* static pods, but it does impact updated static pods which are typically modelled as delete -> recreate (for various reasons) and pods that are created after static pods.  This is similar to #104824 in that the Kubelet needs to be very careful when performing admission to correctly account for *all* resources in use, not just the list of desired pods.  Finally, because we perform pod name exclusion on pods (we don't run two pods with different UIDs but the same pod fullname at the same time), we should also consider the impact of admitting a pod that maps to another pod by full name - it will not be running at the same time.  This is most relevant for force deleted pods - a new one can be created and rescheduled to the same node and cannot start until the old po

title: Support inter-Pod affinity to one or more Pods
body:
In the current implementation of inter-Pod affinity, the scheduler looks for a single existing pod that can satisfy all the terms of inter-pod affinity of an incoming pod.
With the recent changes made to the implementation of inter-Pod affinity, we can now support multiple pods satisfying inter-pod affinity. One of the main reasons we didn't pursue the idea before was the fact that the inter-pod affinity feature was very slow (3 orders of magnitude slower than other scheduler predicates). We didn't want to add more complication to an already slow predicate. However, we can now think about adding the feature.
With this feature, a pod can have multiple affinity terms satisfied by a group of pods, as opposed to only a single pod. For example:

```
- Assume that the cluster has two nodes: 
- nodeA located in in zone1/region1
- nodeB located in zone2/region1

- There are two existing pods on these nodes:
- Pod1:
    - nodeName: "nodeA"
    - label "foo":""

- Pod2:
    - nodeName: "nodeB"
    - label "bar":""

- Pod3 comes in with inter-pod affinity:
    - affinity terms:
        - {label "foo" exists, topologyKey: "region"}
        - {label "bar" exists, topologyKey: "zone"}
```

With our current (K8s 1.12) implementation, Pod3 is not schedulable, because there is no single pod that satisfies all of its affinity terms. However, if we support multiple pods satisfying the affinity terms, Pod3 can be scheduled on nodeB. Pod1 satisfies the first term of its affinity in region1 and Pod2 satisfies its second term in zone2. So, any node in zone2/region1 will be feasible for Pod3.

Given the current implementation of inter-pod affinity and the use of "Topology Pair Maps", I believe implementing this feature requires little changes and won't have noticeable performance impact.

/kind feature
/sig scheduling

cc/ @Huang-Wei @ahmad-diaa

title: Improve readiness times for clusters that use envelope encryption and create large numbers of secrets.
body:
**What would you like to be added**:
Remove the need to call remote KMS for every new Secret.

**Why is this needed**:
Due to the serial processing of List requests, the initialization of informers may take significant time due to the large number of consecutive trips to KMS. For example, assuming a 40 milliseconds round-trip to a KMS and two thousand secrets, the initialization of an informer may take 80 seconds.

Relevant PRs:
Reduce the number of trips to KMS by caching DEKs. #87438
Transform from storage concurrently during List operation. #88633

title: AppArmor validator: Use up to date host info
body:
This issue is created by this @SergeyKanzhelev's [request](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/115749#issuecomment-1441305000)

Currently AppArmor validator gets host info only [when Validator object is created](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/security/apparmor/validate.go#L44).
`Validator.ValidateHost` API [uses cached data](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/security/apparmor/validate.go#L85).

Would it make sense to do it dynamically every time ValidateHost is called? It would help to get the latest AppArmor status, which can be changed if AppArmor kernel module is loaded or unloaded.

title: Mark net.ipv4.ip_local_reserved_ports as a safe sysctl
body:
### What would you like to be added?

The `net.ipv4.ip_local_reserved_ports` sysctl is namespaced so should be safe to permit. It is an often necessary counterpart to `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` sysctl which is currently in the default safe list. It would therefore be helpful to include it in the default safe list as well.

### Why is this needed?

If you have a pod with multiple containers which both sets the `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` to a large range such as the commonly used '1025 65535' in order to maximise the number of available ports *and* binds to local ports in that range then it is possible for a container doing a bind to deadlock repeatedly failing to start if the another container has already used the local port as an ephemeral port. If the ports needed by the bind can be added to the reserved ports list then this issue can be avoided without having to unnecessarily shrink the local port range or add coupling to ensure containers start in the correct order to prevent the deadlock.

title: Cannot create ingress with ingressClass annotation and IngressClassName both set
body:
### What happened?

An ingress resource with both `kubernetes.io/ingress.class` annotation and `spec.ingressClassName` set cannot be **created**. Ingress resources can be updated to include both the annotation and the `ingressClassName` without issue.

Kubernetes response:

> The Ingress "example-ingress" is invalid: annotations.kubernetes.io/ingress.class: Invalid value: "nginx": can not be set when the class field is also set



### What did you expect to happen?

The ingress should be deployed with both annotation and `spec.ingressClassName` set, as it is supported by updating an existing ingress.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Apply this resource:

```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: example-ingress
  annotations:
    ingress.kubernetes.io/rewrite-target: /
    kubernetes.io/ingress.class: "nginx"
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  rules:
  - host: test.foo.bar
    http:
      paths:
        - path: /
          pathType: Prefix
          backend:
            service:
              name: dummy-service
              port:

```

title: Cacher may not send events if it reinitializes at the time of watch initialization
body:
Found when reviewing https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/116024

I'm still not 100% convinced it's true, but I believe this is a faulty scenario:
1. new watch is being established `Watch()` method
2. `c.ready` is still initialized so we successfully pass the c.ready.wait() check
3. `ListAndWatch` in `startCaching` fails (for whatever reason)
4. `c.ready.set(false)` is called (from defer in `startCaching`)
5. `startCaching` is called again and we call `terminateAllWatchers()`
6. the Watch call (started in point 1 above) only now continues to be processed and is established (and added to watchers) - init events are being send in the meantime
7. `ListAndWatch` is being called from `startCaching` which reinitializes watchCache to a new (higher RV)
8. if some events missed in the meantime, they will not be delivered to this newly established watch

/kind bug
/priority critical-urgent
/sig api-machinery

A pod deletion did not result in the correct sandbox pause container being deleted. This was found during internal EKS testing on 1.22, where the test case was as follows:
1. Create a deployment with ~20 replicas and target a single Linux node.
2. Wait for all pods to have networking resources allocated
3. Delete the deployment
4. Validate that networking resources are cleaned up

What is unique about this test is that each pod sandbox fails to get an IP address assigned on average ~100 times before succeeding. So kubelet keeps trying to setup a pod sandbox using a new container ID each time. title: Transition running deleted pods to a terminal phase
body:
### What happened?

Running pods when deleted are not transitioned to a terminal phase, even when all containers are terminated. Note that, containers are not restarted for deleted pods: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/container/helpers.go#L73-L77.

This is problematic for jobs, which as a workaround categorizes all deleted pods (with `deletionTimestamp != nil`) as failed,
but it is still problematic:
- the replacement pod is created too early, leaving two running pods (for the same index) at the same time, which is a problem for some job frameworks. See related Issue: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/115844.
- a pod categorized a failed by the job controller (due to the presence of deletionTimestamp) may end up succeeded if the pod's container completes successfully within the graceful termination period. 
- it blocks a related issue in Jobs: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/113855.

The solution might be scoped to pods with finalizers to save a PATCH request to make the transitioning. 

Fixing this issue is planned as part of the Jobs KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/3329

### What did you expect to happen?

Every deleted running pod is transitioned to a terminal phase if there is a finalizer.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a pod like this:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: running-pod
  finalizers: ["example.com/my-finalizer"]
spec:
  restartPolicy: Always
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: centos:7
    command: ["bash"]
    args: ["-c", 'echo "Hello world" && sleep 1800']
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```
2. Delete the pod by `kubectl delete`
After 30s check the pod status with `kubectl get pods -oyaml`. You can see:

```yaml
    containerStatuses:
    - ...
      state:
        terminated:
          exitCode: 137
          reason: Error
    phase: Running

body:
### What happened?

When I create ServiceAccount as a child resource of other resources, and delete the parent resource, the ServiceAccount did not get deleted.

To illustrate I made a small demo based on [this official blog](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2021/05/14/using-finalizers-to-control-deletion/#owner-references):

A parent ConfigMap:

```console

> apiVersion: v1
> kind: ConfigMap
> metadata:
>   name: mymap-parent
> EOF
configmap/mymap-parent created
```
Get the uid of the parent ConfigMap:

```console
$ CM_UID=$(kubectl get configmap mymap-parent -o jsonpath="{.metadata.uid}")
```

A child ConfigMap:

```console

> apiVersion: v1
> kind: ConfigMap

>   name: mymap-child

>     kind: ConfigMap
>     name: mymap-parent
>     uid: $CM_UID
> EOF
configmap/mymap-child created
```

A child ServiceAccount:

```console

>   name: mysa-child
>   ownerReferences:

>     kind: ConfigMap
>     name: mymap-parent

List the ConfigMaps:

title: No need to check 100 times misses of cronjob
body:
### What would you like to be added?

In v1beta version of cronjob, we checked the missed schedule count in order to avoid excessive looping.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/e8462b5b5dc2584fdcd18e6bcfe9f1e4d970a529/pkg/controller/cronjob/utils.go#L124-L143

Nowadays, however, we do not have looping so I think there is no clear reason for checking 100 times of schedule misses.
We can delete this check in order to simplify the specification.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/cronjob/utils.go#L91-L93

p.s.
The cronjob document says a cronjob does not start a job after reaching 100 times of schedule misses.
Actually the v1 cronjob starts jobs after 100 times of schedule misses, so we should at least revise the document.
https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/cron-jobs/#cron-job-limitations

### Why is this needed?

To simplify the specification.

body:

title: kube-scheduler: Bring back the ability to stop at the first failed filter
body:
#108829 changed the default behavior of scheduler framework's `RunFilterPlugins` - from stopping at the first failed filter to always running all filters. This change breaks Cluster Autoscaler at scale. Cluster Autoscaler imports the scheduler framework to simulate filters on artificial nodes. In a (pretty common) one-pod-per-node scenario, the number of `RunFilterPlugins` calls is ~quadratic wrt. the number of nodes needed for unschedulable pods - it can be a lot of calls. Before #108829, in such scenario the vast majority of `RunFilterPlugins` calls would stop at failing Fit or NodeAffinity filters, and not run the rest of them (e.g. PV-related filters). After the change, every call to `RunFilterPlugins` runs all filters, which completely breaks Cluster Autoscaler at scale (an example scenario of 300 1-pod-per-node pods and 200 node groups takes >10min in 1.24, and ~50s in <1.22).

Can we get the old behavior back? Or re-introduce the config option so that Cluster Autoscaler can set it accordingly? Ideally, we'd also like to get this backported as far as possible (the change was introduced in 1.24).

title: Mutation of a cached object in kubelet through in place resizing of pods
body:
### What happened?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/76d351065e504e23b7962158ef0e9067b6bd96ed/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L2682

mutates the pod object in place (vs creating a copy first).  That's illegal and can cause data races or potentially panics (the panic is unlikely here but I can't rule it out).

This line should be:

```
pod = updatedPod
...
kl.podManager.UpdatePod(pod)
```

This should be fixed because we might serialize the object in the middle of this from somewhere else and if the object changes midway the protobuf object we create may not be valid, leading to panics in kubelets with this gate turned on.

/priority critical-urgent
/kind bug
/assign @vinaykul

No mutation of pod objects from within `Sync*Pod` methods (in fact no mutation of `pod` should occur in most loops).

title: Terminate a Job from an external controller
body:
### What would you like to be added?

/sig apps
/wg batch
/area batch

A mechanism to terminate a Job from an external controller, ensuring all the running pods are deleted.

Potentially, we could simply use a terminal Job condition as a signal.
This could be implemented by enhancing the orphan pod worker to issue pod Deletions when the owner Job is marked as finished. This behavior would be in addition to removing the finalizers when the pods terminate.

### Why is this needed?

Today, simply setting a terminal Job condition (Completed, Failed) might leave Pods running indefinitely (or until `ttlSecondsAfterFinished` is satisfied, if defined), if the controller doesn't have a chance to issue Pod deletions first.

title: pod with CreateContainerConfigError not restarted after stateful set update
body:
### What happened?

1. I  applied a StatefulSet config which references in spec.template.spec.containers[0].env[i].valueFrom.secretKeyRef.name a secret, that doesn't exist. A corresponding pod is started but runs into CreateContainerConfigError.
2. I fixed the StatefulSet config by removing the corresponding spec.template.spec.containers[0].env[i] element and applied the new config.

Unexpected: The reduced env is not updated in the pod yaml. The pod remains stuck in CreateContainerConfigError state.

### What did you expect to happen?

I expect the pod to be restarted when its stateful set is modified.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Fix stateful set by adding a reference to your favorite image (any image should do) and create the set.
Do NOT create the secret `mysql-credentials`.
```yaml
kind: StatefulSet
apiVersion: apps/v1
metadata:
  name: mysql
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: mysql-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: mysql-app
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: mysql

title: automated testing of command line interfaces
body:
#### What would you like to be added:

We should have pre-merge tests that verify that code changes do not affect the command line interface of the Kubernetes tools. This could cover:
- which flags are supported (removing flags is a breaking change)
- formatting of help texts (hyphen versus underscore for legacy flags)
- error handling when the command line is invalid (ideally the usage text should get printed, followed by the error)

The script from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/105076#issuecomment-931319645 might serve as starting point.

#### Why is this needed:

The command line API is part of the Kubernetes API and must be kept stable. Removing flags must be done with proper deprecation. Adding flags should not be done lightly.

title: Allow for additional information to be passed in AdmissionResponse object to the Kubernetes CLI
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Currently, the Result field of the [AdmissionsResponse](https://github.com/kubernetes/api/blob/master/admission/v1/types.go#L127) is not consulted if the Admission Controller allows the object. It would be helpful to developers if certain admission controller response messages could be displayed, even on successes.



### Why is this needed?

When maintaining production environments, it can often be useful to communicate things that are not precisely warnings back to the end user. While you can use the Warnings field, all of these messages end up with Warning: prefixes and not everything that an admission controller wants to communicate is a Warning.

Or, perhaps there is a more recommended way of communicating information to the CLI on success not in a warning that I've missed?

/sig CLI

/sig api-machinery

title: Panic Threshold for Readiness Probe Failures
body:
### What would you like to be added?

When using external dependencies inside healthchecks or using fixed thread pool applications like python+gunicorn, ruby+passenger, PHP etc,...  upstream service failures tend to cause cascading impact on the service as well.

one solution is removing the upstream services inside the healthchecks and that's how we are solving currently but that still won't solve the case where healthchecks are failing due to excessive load. like suddenly 2x requests came on service that caused some pods to reach capacity and start failing readiness probes which in turn causes a cascading impact where scheduler removes the pods from the service.

we faced similar issues in envoy and unhealthy panic threshold in envoy helped a lot - https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/intro/arch_overview/upstream/load_balancing/panic_threshold

the feature has a lot of moving parts though i.e it shouldn't trigger during normal scenarios like deployments, rotating the pods of a service, interruptions in the underlying ec2 leading to replacements of pods in significant chunks.

references to similar outages - 
1. https://loft.sh/blog/kubernetes-readiness-probes-examples-and-common-pitfalls/#cascading-failures
2. https://doordash.engineering/2022/08/09/how-to-handle-kubernetes-health-checks/

### Why is this needed?

To avoid cascading outages when more than 30-40% of the pods of a deployment starts failing readiness probes

title: kube-proxy IPVS mode: traffic sent from pods to an external LoadBalancer IP is NOT directed to the respective cluster IP instead
body:
### What happened?


According to the [docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/command-line-tools-reference/kube-proxy/#:~:text=will%20be%20masqueraded%20and-,traffic%20sent%20from%20pods%20to%20an%20external%20LoadBalancer%20IP%20will%20be%20directed%20to%20the%20respective%20cluster%20IP%20instead.,-For%20dual)  

> traffic sent from pods to an external LoadBalancer IP will be directed to the respective cluster IP instead

But in fact it's not the case for kube-proxy running in IPVS mode.

### What did you expect to happen?


This is kind of "breaking change" that IPVS mode brings - **pods running on the nodes, where there are no pods which Loadbalancer IP's related service points to, are capable to access that service by External IP (e.g. Ingresses that are resolved in DNS to LoadBalancer IP)**:
1. only if `ExternalTrafficPolicy` for related service is set to `Cluster`
2. only via SrcNAT loosing their IPs in logs

There are no such limitaions with kube-proxy in `iptables` mode which provide redirection to ClusterIP mentioned above via iptables rules with comments like _"Redirect pods trying to reach external loadbalancer VIP to clusterIP"_

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Any installation with kube-proxy in IPVS mode

title: kubectl does not have a way to adjust its client-side rate limiting
body:
### What happened?

kubectl does client-side rate limiting, but the limit is not adjustable.  This is inappropriately inflexible and commonly results in annoying error messages.  There is no inherently correct setting for client self-restraint; what is reasonable for one client depends on all the other clients and the servers.

A colleague preparing a demo using a kind cluster complained "this happens every time I get a CR", showing the following typescript.

```
kubectl get xsqldatabases.multicloud.aether.io       
I0615 16:05:15.481530 1384109 request.go:665] Waited for 1.179551114s due to client-side throttling, not priority and fairness, request: GET:https://127.0.0.1:33063/apis/cache.aws.crossplane.io/v1alpha1?timeout=32s

body:
### What happened?

The docker images for linux/arm64 wrongly report their architecture as amd64. This issue affects at least the `v1.8.6` and `v1.9.3` of the coredns images.


### What did you expect to happen?

Expected the arm64 version of the image to correctly report its architecture as arm64.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

## 1) Pull the image, specifying the linux/arm64 platform.
```bash
> docker pull --platform linux/arm64 registry.k8s.io/coredns/coredns:v1.8.6

v1.8.6: Pulling from coredns/coredns
Digest: sha256:5b6ec0d6de9baaf3e92d0f66cd96a25b9edbce8716f5f15dcd1a616b3abd590e
Status: Image is up to date for registry.k8s.io/coredns/coredns:v1.8.6
registry.k8s.io/coredns/coredns:v1.8.6
```

## 2) Inspect the image for the digest linked to the specified platform.
```bash
> docker inspect -f '{{.Architecture}}' registry.k8s.io/coredns/coredns:v1.8.6@sha256:5b6ec0d6de9baaf3e92d0f66cd96a25b9edbce8716f5f15dcd1a616b3abd590e

amd64
```

The above images is not showing the correct architecture. 

Note that this issue is sometimes silent when using MacOS as the platform does support running amd64 images. e.g. `kind` can create a working cluster even with the wrong image arch. However, using e.g. `kind load` will fail as there is an architecture check when this command is run.

### What would you like to be added?

`kubeadm init phase certs` needs to take the "Validity  > NotBefore" from current date/time of the system . to keep the life time of certificate one year.

### Why is this needed?

If we have any renewal for the API-Server certificate  ( like renew of API-Server in AWS EKS cluster , because of the Control Plane instance refresh ) , the "Validity  > NotBefore" will stay as the creation time of the cluster and CA, but the new API-Certificate expiry time ( "Validity  > NotAfter" ) will update to keep the certificate life to one year from this renewal .
It is causing the duration from "Validity  > NotBefore"  to "Validity  > NotAfter" will be more than one year .

title: Optimize scheduler's FitError
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Scheduler's [FitError](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b2ed6ca64f55452cdb4063d62920dddccd4344f7/pkg/scheduler/framework/types.go#L223) wraps info to diagose a pod's scheduler failure. The object is dumped to system event, and also injected into a pod's status. However, the way FitError is currently dealt with is not efficient in the following aspects:

### 1. Unnecessary compose/decompose

When a FitError gets wrapped into a Status, it's achieved by:
- `framework.NewStatus(..., err.Error())`, or
- `framework.AsStatus(err)`

The first function decomposed the err, and composed [another](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5583f0c0659b4033869939ad4c8ee3bca156386b/pkg/scheduler/framework/interface.go#L246) error.
The second function, although injects the err into the Status, it calls [err.Error()](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5583f0c0659b4033869939ad4c8ee3bca156386b/pkg/scheduler/framework/interface.go#L255) which should be lazy-evaluted.

The optimization should try to reuse the same FitError as much as possible, and also delay its evaluation (i.e., call FitError.Error()).

### 2. Duplicated calls to FitError.Error()

Suppose we have solved the problems mentioned above, and hence have a unique FitError across one scheduling cycle, the current logic that calls `FitError.Error()` multiple times are still problematic. Currently it may be called ~4~ 3 times during a scheduling cycle:

- ~composing a PostFilter status ([A](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5583f0c0659b4033869939ad4c8ee3bca156386b/pkg/scheduler/framework/preemption/preemption.go#L173))~
- duplicated entries when dealing with the error ([B](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5583f0c0659b4033869939ad4c8ee3bca156386b/pkg/scheduler/schedule_one.go#L813), [C](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5583f0c0659b4033869939ad4c8ee3bca156386b/pkg/scheduler/schedule_one.go#L824), [D](https://

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:

* PVC was created, & pod consuming this PVC. PVC is using the WaitForFirstConsumer policy. 
* controller with SA `persistent-volume-binder` in `kube-system` namespace edited the PVC, attached the following labels:

```
    volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-provisioner: ebs.csi.aws.com
    volume.kubernetes.io/selected-node: ip-10-0-92-212.ec2.internal
```
* PVC is pending phase, it wasn't bound to the PV. 
* The node in question was deleted, by cluster autoscaler 1.20 before the PV was provisioned and attached to the node. 
* The annotation remains
* The https://github.com/kubernetes/autoscaler/tree/master/cluster-autoscaler v1.20 cannot scale up the node since there's the `volume.kubernetes.io/selected-node` annotation pointing to the deleted node. The cluster autoscaler sees this PVC bound to the Pod already bound to the node, but the node isn't there. 
* The pod stays forever in pending state
* Deleting this annotation allows cluster autoscaler to do its job, scaling up the cluster and the pod gets scheduled on a newly provisioned node. 
* The end. 

#### What you expected to happen:

* Upon node deletion, the `volume.kubernetes.io/selected-node` annotation should be cleared.

title: Filesystem resize is required after snapshot restore / volume clone
body:
Kubernetes should resize filesystem on a volume when it's created as a clone of a smaller volume / smaller snapshot is restored into it.

Example:
1. User takes a snapshot of 1 GiB volume with ext3 filesystem on it.
2. User restores the snapshot into 2 GiB volume.
    2.1 CSI driver restores the snapshot into a bigger volume, but ext3 filesystem still uses only 1 GiB of space.
3. CSI driver should make sure that the filesystem on the volume has been resized before the volume is mounted into a pod.

There are few steps needed:

* [x] Clarify behavior of `CreateVolume` CSI call, https://github.com/container-storage-interface/spec/pull/452
* [ ] Update CSI drivers to the new behavior.
  * [x] Move filesystem resize code from kubernetes/kuberenetes to kubernetes/mount-utils, so all CSI drivers can re-use the same code https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/99039 
  * [x] Enhance the code above to compare the volume size from block device perspective and from filesystem perspective. See https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/aws-ebs-csi-driver/pull/595 for proof of concept. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/99042
  * [ ] File issues in all community CSI drivers that we care about & fix them.
* [ ] Update csi-tests to (optionally?) check for volume size when cloning / restoring snapshot to a bigger size. https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/csi-test/issues/325

title: Expose image digest in pull image event
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Extend the event message with the concrete image digest in a kubelet's successful pull event: `Successfully pulled image "nginx@sha256:df13abe416e37eb3db4722840dd479b00ba193ac6606e7902331dcea50f4f1f2" as "nginx:1.19" in 2.5610178s` if a container's image was not specified using a digest.

### Why is this needed?

# Problem Statement

When a pod is created and the image property for a container is specified using a tag (`busybox:1.34`) or merely the name (`busybox`) the container runtime will pull the image on a node. If a pod is being recreated (due to its container's process crashing for example) and the tag has been moved to new revision (e.g. `busybox:1.34.1`) in the registry, a new image will be pulled. The user could end up running an unexpected change or different revisions within a deployment, while this change of revision is mostly intransparent to the user.

# Suggested Solution

Events do record the occurance of a resolve-pull event (`Successfully pulled image \"nginx:latest\" in 1.9053881s"`), while k8s events are usually ephemeral, additional cluster components however are able to watch and record events to process and store them further for usage in forensics or observability. It would be possible to modify the event message to expose the full digest to which a pulled image has been resolved.

# Alternative Remedies

## ImagePullPolicy

Specifying `imagePullPolicy=IfNotPresent` will not help, it will merely avoid re-pulling an image if an image with the given tag is already present on a node. If that's not the case, it will still be pulled.

## Admission Controllers

An admission controller component could resolve image tags to their respective digest and modify a pod's specification before it is admitted to the cluster. Alternatively admission controllers could reject `image` properties without a digest suffix. It's a good option to avoid the problem on a cluster level, but beyond the control of a c

title: Update cli-runtime to Kustomize v5
body:
### What happened?

Please update the Kustomize packages in cli-runtime to  `sigs.k8s.io/kustomize/api@v0.13.1` and `sigs.k8s.io/kustomize/kyaml@v0.14.0`. Every project that imports both `cli-runtime` and the new `kustomize/api` result in compilation error due to the removal of `DoLegacyResourceSort` which is used in cli-runtime here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cli-runtime/pkg/resource/kustomizevisitor.go#L41.

Bumping `sigs.k8s.io/kustomize/api` to `v0.13.1` results in:

```
# k8s.io/cli-runtime/pkg/resource
../../../../pkg/mod/k8s.io/cli-runtime@v0.26.1/pkg/resource/kustomizevisitor.go:41:8:
kOpts.DoLegacyResourceSort undefined (type *krusty.Options has no field or method DoLegacyResourceSort)
```

title: Allow scaling up to meet PDB constraints
body:
**What would you like to be added**:

Currently if you have a PDB spec like `minAvailable: 1`, and a HPA defining minReplicas=1 and maxReplicas=N, you may end up in a scenario where disruptions get "stuck" if the HPA has scaled to 1. At any point an increase in load could cause the HPA to scale up to 2+, allowing the PDB to be satisfied, which leads to a weird scenario where a disruption can only occur if there is high load.

Ideally, the PDB would be able to trigger the HPA to scale up to meet constraints. For example, if I have 1 replica and a disruption is triggered, scale up a new replica first, then terminate the old one. Given an HPA is in place, I have already clearly specified I am OK with my pod being scaled up, so this shouldn't have negative impact on stateful workloads.

Some more context: https://github.com/istio/istio/issues/12602

title: Incorrect and misleading error reporting: failed to initialize top level QOS containers: root container [kubepods] doesn't exist
body:
### What happened?

When doing validation, kubernetes doesn't actually report the issue with the cgroup kupepods, instead they issue an error that cgroup kubepods doesn't exist at all. This is related to opencontainers not checking if controllers got properly set:
https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/issues/3647

So it goes like this:
Kubernetes use opencontainers to set up cgroup kubepods.
Opencontainers doesn't check if anything actually succeeded.
Then later Kubernetes check if everything is configured correctly during validation and when anything is even slightly out of the ordinary, it shreds any information what is wrong, and instead it reports that kubepods doesn't exist at all.

### What did you expect to happen?

I would assume software not lying. When kubepods exist, the Kubernetes should not lie that it doesn't and if it knows what it is missing, it should report it and not silently throw it away.

title: [Winkernel Proxier] No ingress load balancer rules with endpoints to support load balancing when all the endpoints are terminating
body:
### What happened?

HNS requires the Load Balancing Policy to be configured to identify the traffic destined to a cloud providers Load Balancer IP (VIP) and forward it to the distributed Load Balancer running in VFP on the node. Windows Kube-proxy ignores the terminating endpoints and strictly creates a HNS Load Balancer policy only for "Ready" pods that are not terminating. This creates a problem when all the PODs serving as backends for a Service are terminating. The traffic for active connections is not delivered to the Distributed LoadBalancer and dropped on the Windows node.

### What did you expect to happen?

Windows Kube-proxy/HNS should handle the terminating endpoints correctly to minimize the network traffic loss.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a Service of Type LoadBalancer with exactly one POD as a backend.
2. Establish a long running TCP connection from an external Client to the Service.
3. Scale the deployment to delete the POD.
4. The active connection is immediately broken. A prestop hook handler configured on the POD will not get a chance to gracefully terminate the connection.

### Kubernetes version

1.24.0 and above

### Cloud provider

Azure Kubernetes Service

### OS version

Windows Server 2019, Windows Server 2022

Following my comment [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/14188#issuecomment-952935754), I think it would be very useful to expose the value of `spec.completions` to the containers. The same way that it is currently done for the completion index. 

### Why is this needed?

We have recently started to use the indexed jobs to process data on one of our clusters. When the pods are aware of both the completions and their own completion index, it is pretty trivial for the them to dispatch/slice the work without any central scheduler or queue.
Unfortunately, it is not trivial to pass to the containers environments since it is part of the Job spec and as such is not available through the downward API.

@alculquicondor @soltysh 

PS: If this is going to be implemented, you might as well expose both `spec.completions` and `spec.parallelism`. I can see situations where it might be useful for the pod to be aware of how many pods are running beside it.

title: CSI volumes left overs are not cleaned up if CSI plugin is attachable
body:
### What happened?

1. Create a Deployment or SS that uses a vsphere CSI volumes (for example).
2. Shutdown the node while pod was running.
3. Wait for node to go `NotReady` and pod to switch to `Terminating` state. 
4. Bring back the node up.
5. If the pod migrates to different node (or pod gets deleted), then files/directories inside `/var/lib/kubelet/pods/xxxx` should be cleaned up.

The reason those directories are not being cleaned up is because:

1. The volume types that are attachable, kubelet expects `node-publish-path` to be a mount point during reconstruction. So if node is rebooted then reconstruction fails because `/mount` path is not a mount point.
2. Kubelet tries to "Cleanup" the volume, but CSI driver may be unavailable at this point.
3. As a result volumes are never cleaned up.





### What did you expect to happen?

Expected cleanup to happen properly.

See above

title: Memory leak in kubelet volume_manager populator processedPods
body:
### What happened?

If a pod is created and then deleted an entry in processedPods map remains forever (sometimes, it's racy).

The problem comes from the fact that `podWorker` calls volume_manager `WaitForUnmount()` asynchronously. If the last call happens after populator cleaned up resources, an entry is added to processedPods and will never be seen.

### What did you expect to happen?

An entry in processedPods map must be deleted if pod doesn't exist and pod runtime should removed according to `dswp.podStateProvider`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

To verify that the issue really exists I applaied a simple [patch](https://github.com/jsafrane/kubernetes/commit/40ffc8e62836244ea6cffde8b9dff2c402d058c5) printing resources in `processedPods` map. Here is a reproducer:

title: Investigating detecting GOMAXPROCS based on cgroup values
body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:

`make test` should detect the appropriate GOMAXPROCS based off of the cpu limit supplied to the pod.  

**Why is this needed**:


If not, test failures can occur (e.g. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/116990) where GOMAXPROCS defaults to the number of cpus on the machine, while the cpu limit is actually far less.  Too many compile/test processes launch, and any timing tests can become flaky. The end result is that running the test jobs on a node with more CPUs can make it flaky when running the test on a node with fewer CPUs cleanly passes.

It's possible to set GOMAXPROCS=cpu limits in test jobs to avoid this, but it would be nicer if `make test` would autodiscover and set GOMAXPROCS appropriately.

title: `volume.SetVolumeOwnership()` always fails when called for wrapped volume
body:
### What happened?

Every time `volume.SetVolumeOwnership(ed)` from `empty_dir.go` is called for a projected volume, it fails with "no such file or directory" error.

The problem comes from the fact that `SetVolumeOwnership()` always calculates the root dir for ownership changes as `mounter.GetPath()` while projected.go explicitly passes another dir as the first arg of `SetUpAt()` call:
```
	if err := wrapped.SetUpAt(dir, mounterArgs); err != nil {
		return err
	}
```
(see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/96306f144a3c917a97fe27c9ad5dd89e4213f741/pkg/volume/projected/projected.go#L203)

### What did you expect to happen?

`volume.SetVolumeOwnership()` must succeed when a projected volume is created.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Print return value of `volume.SetVolumeOwnership()` when called from `empty_dir.go`:
```
diff --git a/pkg/volume/emptydir/empty_dir.go b/pkg/volume/emptydir/empty_dir.go
index 9ad981c54bd..ce3f7d330fe 100644
--- a/pkg/volume/emptydir/empty_dir.go
+++ b/pkg/volume/emptydir/empty_dir.go
@@ -280,7 +280,10 @@ func (ed *emptyDir) SetUpAt(dir string, mounterArgs volume.MounterArgs) error {
                err = fmt.Errorf("unknown storage medium %q", ed.medium)
        }
 
-       volume.SetVolumeOwnership(ed, mounterArgs.FsGroup, nil /*fsGroupChangePolicy*/, volumeutil.FSGroupCompleteHook(ed.plugin, nil))
+       e := volume.SetVolumeOwnership(ed, mounterArgs.FsGroup, nil /*fsGroupChangePolicy*/, volumeutil.FSGroupCompleteHook(ed.plugin, nil))
+       if e != nil {
+               klog.Infof("ZZZ: SetVolumeOwnership() returned error: %v (dir: %v; ed.GetPath(): %v)", e, dir, ed.GetPath())
+       }
 
        // If setting up the quota fails, just log a message but don't actually error out.
        // We'll use the old du mechanism in this case, at least until we support
```

Start an arbitrary pod, then look at kubelet logs:
```
$ kubectl apply -f fedora.yaml

$

title: Edge case - job pods nearing completion being evicted even though protected by PodDisruptionBudget
body:
### What happened?

I believe I've come across an edge case in evictions which can cause job pods to be evicted and replaced even though they complete without error.

Here's the scenario:

- Create a job with `completions` and `parallelism` both set to 3.
- Add a PodDisruptionBudget in place for this job's pods, with `minAvailable` set to 3.
- All three pods are created and run successfully without crashing or hitting an `activeDeadlineSeconds` deadline.
- Just around the time the pods are about to complete their work and move from `Running` to `Completed`, one of them is selected for eviction by the [Descheduler](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/descheduler)
- The eviction is successful, and results in a replacement pod being created.

In terms of frequency, we don't see this problem often - perhaps a couple of times over hundreds of jobs - but it is a persistent issue that we've seen over months.

### What did you expect to happen?

I would expect a replacement pod not to have been created, as all three pods appear to have completed successfully, and the PodDisruptionBudget should protect them from a descheduler-triggered eviction.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

I've come up with a crude reproducible testcase that shows the problem roughly 4 out of 5 times against a [kind](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io) cluster. It's automated in the shell script below. Obviously I don't have the descheduler running in that kind cluster, so I have a repeated loop of eviction attempts (via the [kubectl-evict plugin](https://github.com/ueokande/kubectl-evict)) which I think exhibits the same behaviour as a descheduler-initiated eviction attempt happening at the appropriate point to trigger to issue.

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash

kubectl --context kind create ns troubleshooting
kubectl --context kind -n troubleshooting delete job/my-test-job pdb/my-test-job-pdb

cat << EOF | kubectl --context kind -n troubleshooting apply -f -
apiV

title: kubelet issues when LocalStorageCapacityIsolationFSQuotaMonitoring is enabled
body:
### What happened?

1. When the flag is enabled quota setup fails on subsequent invocations

Each time quota is applied on a volume, a new random UUID for the pod is generated and this UUID is compared with the previous stored one internally. If it doesn't match then the whole process stops and an error is returned.

2. ConfigMaps and secrets volume update fail and it floods the cluster with error events

ConfigMaps and secrets use emptyDir volumes which try to reapply quotas on every invocation. Since quota setup fails on subsequent invocations an error is logged each time and the process of updating the payloads is stopped. This happens frequently and it floods the cluster with error messages.

```
kube-system   68s         Warning   FailedMount               pod/kube-proxy-nmmnq                                                (combined from similar events): MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "kube-proxy" : requesting quota on existing directory /mnt/kubelet/pods/e9f869de-fdf4-4728-a969-34abdaf00683/volumes/kubernetes.io~configmap/kube-proxy but different pod f61ddb8b-82cf-480c-910c-9adbcc643bb2 4e06badc-1093-4076-a127-267aa27ebd46
```

3. After kubelet restarts trying to apply quota fails because the folder already has a quota project id associated with it.

```
monitoring    11m         Warning   FailedMount               pod/prometheus-monitoring-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0              MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "config-out" : assign quota FAILED createProjectID /mnt/kubelet/pods/ea2780a5-66bb-435c-9395-bf3609839123/volumes/kubernetes.io~empty-dir/config-out 0 failed attempt to reassign project ID for /mnt/kubelet/pods/ea2780a5-66bb-435c-9395-bf3609839123/volumes/kubernetes.io~empty-dir/config-out
```

Similar issues: #114506, #112081

title: Allow ConcurrentJobSyncs to be set for kube-controller-manager
body:
**What would you like to be added**:
The ability to set `ConcurrentJobSyncs` for the kube-controller-manager at runtime.  It looks like the option exists in the code, but a mechanism is not available to set it via kops.  If I understand the code correctly, a flag needs to be added in order to be able to set the value using kops.

**Why is this needed**:
We want to shift a lot of our batch processing jobs from running directly on our CI servers to running as jobs on Kubernetes.  Unfortunately if too many jobs are launched on kubernetes, they begin to back up. ### What happened?

According to the official document https://kubernetes.io/blog/2021/08/27/minreadyseconds-statefulsets/, The pod available time point is `ready lastTransitionTime + minReadySecond`. However, I found a wired phenomenon when using it(does not configure readiness prober and the pod changes to the ready status fast). The difference between the AGE of sts-0 and the AGE of sts-1 is about twice the value of minReadySecond, and the difference between the AGE of sts-1 and the AGE of sts-2 is also twice the value of minReadySecond. By this logic, the difference between the AGE of sts-5 and the AGE of sts-0 will be 10 times the value of minReadySecond.

set minReadySecond=30, PodManagementPolicyType = OrderedReady

title: RuntimeClass based scheduling alternation doesn't work for DaemonSet
body:
### What happened?

Daemonset's predictate doesn't look into RuntimeClass's scheduling section, which can be a problem in two scenarios:

1. Pods never created, due to a toleration marked in RuntimeClass but not in the spec.template.
2. Pods get created, but stuck in pending due to a nodeSelector marked in RuntimeClass, but not in spec.template.


### What did you expect to happen?

Either we should be warned not to use runtimeClass for daemonsets, or (preferably) daemonsets should do what's necessary to correctly interpret RuntimeClass scheduling information.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Say I have a below yaml, and nodes as shown:

```
apiVersion: node.k8s.io/v1
kind: RuntimeClass
metadata:
  name: testrc
handler: runc
scheduling:
  nodeSelector:
    # use anything
    kubernetes.io/hostname: aks-nodepool1-58567673-vmss000002
  tolerations:
  - key: "node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable"
    operator: "Exists"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: rctest
  labels:
    app: rctest
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: rctest
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: rctest
    spec:
      runtimeClassName: testrc
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:1.14.2
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
```
