title: reflector relist when api server upgrade
body:
### What happened? My project use istio as a registry, when k8s api server upgrade or restart, the client-go reflector will do relist and watch, and this can result in a large number of duplicate update events(10w+ events) and pilot handl lager duplicate update events(workloadentry), eventually, the update of Routing table is delayed more then some minutes. ### What did you expect to happen? My expectation is that during api server upgrades or when there are occasional timeout disconnects, the client-go reflector should not perform a relist operation, but instead continue to retry the watch to avoid handling a large number of duplicate update events and cause routing table delayed. **And one of my doubts is why the watch operation is only retried when the connention refused, why not when the connection is closed or connection reset by peer or request timeout?** I think it is safe to retry with last resourceVersion when connection close or timeout, but I'm not sure what details I haven't considered. title: apiserver crashes with dual-stack service CIDRs if primary range does not match `kubernetes.default` Public IP family in k8s >= 1.24
body:
### What happened?

apiserver crashes at startup if using dual-stack service CIDRs but the primary service CIDR family does not match the IP family of the advertised address.

#106721 introduced validation that checks the service CIDR is the same IP family as the advertised public address of apiserver. It assumes single-stack scenarios and does not check `ExtraConfig.SecondaryServiceIPRange`

### What did you expect to happen?

This should not block apiserver to come up. AKS has been testing clusters with the IPv6 service CIDR as primary with an IPv4 public IP with no issues until 1.24. Example of the kubernetes default service with IPv6 cluster IP but IPv4 endpoint.

```
Name:              kubernetes
Namespace:         default
Labels:            component=apiserver
                   provider=kubernetes
Annotations:       <none>
Selector:          <none>
Type:              ClusterIP
IP Family Policy:  SingleStack
IP Families:       IPv6
IP:                fdff:ffff:1234:6754::1
IPs:               fdff:ffff:1234:6754::1
Port:              https  443/TCP
TargetPort:        443/TCP
Endpoints:         52.188.128.76:443
Session Affinity:  None
Events:            <none>
```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a dual-stack cluster using k8s 1.24 with an IPv4 public IP and order the service-cluster-ip-range argument to apiserver such that IPv6 is first (e.g. `--service-cluster-ip-range="fdff:ffff:1234:6754::/108,100.64.0.0/16"`. Apiserver will fail to come up with a similar error message

```
I0803 14:48:27.991658       1 flags.go:64] FLAG: --advertise-address="20.21.22.23"
I0803 14:48:27.992806       1 flags.go:64] FLAG: --service-cluster-ip-range="fdff:ffff:1234:6754::/108,100.64.0.0/16"
E0803 14:48:30.149624       1 run.go:74] "command failed" err="error creating bootstrap controller: service IP family \"fdff:ffff:1234:6754::/108\" must match public address family \"20.21.22.23\""

title: upgradeaware proxy and golang httputil.ReverseProxy
body:
Since golang 1.12 https://github.com/golang/go/commit/ee55f0856a3f1fed5d8c15af54c40e4799c2d32f
the standard library httputil.ReverseProxy supports automatic upgrade to websockets and other protocols, in a much cleaner implementation that we have today in `staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/proxy/upgradeaware.go`

Also, a quick look to the golang ReverseProxy history, shows that is well maintained, at least better than our implementation, per example, it has request cancellation for upgrade requests, that is missing here.

https://github.com/golang/go/commits/a10a209b23f877c80d8a5f3ebda1ce4b492ac3a9?before=a10a209b23f877c80d8a5f3ebda1ce4b492ac3a9+35&branch=a10a209b23f877c80d8a5f3ebda1ce4b492ac3a9&path%5B%5D=src&path%5B%5D=net&path%5B%5D=http&path%5B%5D=httputil&path%5B%5D=reverseproxy.go

At first sight is mostly removing code, 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/compare/master...aojea:upgradeware_proxy?expand=1

but there is this `MaxBytesPerSec` capability that may be more complicated to implement.

Is this capability something that can be deprecated?
If not, I think that is worth at least adapt the code to match the standard library as much as possible

title: Adapt swap jobs to run with cgroup v2
body:
**Context**:
NodeSwap feature gate was recently [graduated to Beta1](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4128). Currently, as per [the KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/2400-node-swap), swap is only supported with cgroup v2 - cgroup v1 is no longer supported.

For this reason, we decided to fail kubelet if NodeSwap feature gate is enabled and the node runs with cgroup v1. This would help prevent any surprises for the user by failing as soon as possible. This effort is being implemented in this PR: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119327.

**The problem**:
Currently, swap jobs are running with cgroup v1. Swap tests were added in a way that they first check on which environment they're being run (e.g. which cgroup version? is NodeSwap FG enabled? Which swapBehavior is defined? etc) and then expect the right behavior to take place. With v1, the tests expect the containers to be defined without swap access.

While the tests pass, they are much less valuable, since all they check is that swap is disabled for v1 workloads. The tests would be much more valuable if they would run with v2, therefore actually ensure that proper swap limitations are configured.

In addition, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119327 is dependent on these changes, since as of now the jobs immediately fail with this PR since kubelet fails on an environment with cgroup v1 and swap enabled.

**What needs to change**:
- [ ] CRI-O swap related jobs should be defined to run with cgroup v2 (e.g. `pull-kubernetes-node-swap-fedora`)
  - https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/pull/30242
- [ ] containerd swap related jobs should be defined to run with cgroup v2 (e.g. `pull-kubernetes-node-swap-ubuntu-serial`).
  - https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/pull/30297

**Future work**:
In the future, we might consider introducing more jobs to check swap. Ideally, both `LimitedSwap` and `UnlimitedSwap` would be

title: Restore Kubernetes API service endpoint during HA rolling restarts
body:
### What happened?

I think that https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/115804 via https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/116685 have introduced a regression for HA Kubernetes API server configurations behind a proxy and/or load balancer.  Such configurations may only have a single Kubernetes API server endpoint that should not be removed during a rolling restart of the Kubernetes API server.

**Example:**
```
$  kubectl get endpoints kubernetes --no-headers
kubernetes   172.20.0.1:2040   48m
```

### What did you expect to happen?

`kubectl get endpoints kubernetes --no-headers` will remain unchanged throughout the HA rolling restart of the Kubernetes API server.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run the following script during an HA rolling restart of the Kubernetes API server:

```
while true; do date && kubectl get endpoints kubernetes --no-headers; sleep 1; done
```

You will see `kubectl get endpoints kubernetes --no-headers` return `kubernetes   <none>` several times during this rollout.

title: kube-controller-manager should not cache managedFields
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Remove [`managedFields`](https://github.com/kubernetes/apimachinery/blob/v0.27.2/pkg/apis/meta/v1/types.go#L271) from the cached used by controllers in `kube-controller-manager`. If feasible, this work will be applied to other components having similar use patterns but have no use of `managedFields` at all.

### Why is this needed?

Roughly the content in `managedFields` is a copy of whole object so it takes roughly 40% of total object size, which is a significant memory overhead. Removing it for controllers can improve memory efficiency

title: controller_util_test.go does not follow similar patterns as other unit tests in the repo.
body:
### What would you like to be added?

During implementation of KEP 3393 (PodReplacementPolicy for Jobs) we found that the unit tests of [controller_util_test.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/controller_utils_test.go) do not follow common patterns established in k/k.  

1) The tests are not written using table driven design (https://dave.cheney.net/2019/05/07/prefer-table-driven-tests).

2) The tests use `Differences` rather than `Cmp.Diff`.

This probably should be done as two separate PRs but wanted to highlight some areas that could use some cleanup. 

### Why is this needed?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/117015#discussion_r1254470573

Not using `Cmp.Diff` means that we don't see diffs in the unit tests that makes this difficult.  

And not using table driven tests makes it difficult to add new test cases as it usually is brought up during review that we should use a table-driven test but the entire file does not obey this format.

title: NCC-E003660-PCK: Non Constant-Time Comparison of Service Account Token Secrets
body:
### NCC-E003660-PCK: Non Constant-Time Comparison of Service Account Token Secrets
This issue was reported in the [Kubernetes 1.24 Security Audit Report](https://github.com/kubernetes/sig-security/blob/main/sig-security-external-audit/security-audit-2021-2022/findings/Kubernetes%20v1.24%20Final%20Report.pdf)

**Impact**
An attacker may be able to guess a service account token secret, and impersonate the
affected account to read, modify, or delete application data to which the account has
access in a Kubernetes cluster.

**Description**
Service account token secrets (`kubernetes.io/service-account-token`) are a type of
secret used to authenticate service accounts. The “Service account token Secrets” section
of the Kubernetes “Configuration” documentation does not recommend their usage:

> Since 1.22, this type of Secret is no longer used to mount credentials into Pods, and obtaining tokens via the TokenRequest API is recommended instead of using service account token Secret objects. Tokens obtained from the TokenRequest API are more secure than ones stored in Secret objects, because they have a bounded lifetime and are not readable by other API clients. You can use the `kubectl create token` command to obtain a token from the TokenRequest API.

> You should only create a service account token Secret object if you can’t use the TokenRequest API to obtain a token, and the security exposure of persisting a non-expiring token credential in a readable API object is acceptable to you.

Nevertheless, their usage appears to be possible, and may be employed by Kubernetes
users. The process of creating a service account token is documented in the [“Configure
Service Accounts for Pods” documentation section](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account/).

An incoming service account request is authenticated by first verifying the JWT signature
of the token, then by comparing the secret token value embedd

`PodDisruptionBudget` with an empty selector `{}` selects all the pods as expected.
But, during the `drain` /`eviction`, the pdb is not being honored correctly i.e. all the pods are getting evicted.

This issue is only observed with the empty selector and works as expected if a valid label selector is provided that selects all the pods in a namespace.

### What did you expect to happen?

When an empty selector `{}` is provided in the `PodDisruptionBudget`'s spec, the created `PodDisruptionBudget` needs to be honored by not evicting all the pods during the `drain/eviction` api call

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- Create a simple busybox deployment with 3 replicas on a local cluster (or any cluster)
```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: busybox
  name: busybox
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: busybox
  strategy:
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 25%
      maxUnavailable: 25%
    type: RollingUpdate
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: busybox
    spec:
      containers:
      - image: busybox
        name: busybox
        command: ["sleep", "1000"]
      dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst
      restartPolicy: Always
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30

```
- Create a pdb object with an `empty` selector `{}`
```
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 100%  
  selector: {}
```
- Check the status of the created pdb object that has the `expectedPods` observed to be 3 (which is expected)
```

title: sched: CycleState.SkipFilterPlugins not always injected into cycleState
body:
### What happened?

In k8s 1.27, scheduler introduced a new "short circuit" semantics in PreFilter to bypass a Pod quickly. A change introduced here is it relies on that plugin to be stored in `CycleState.SkipFilterPlugins`, which makes sense as what it was explained [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/114125/files#r1062646736).

However, the `SkipFilterPlugins` info, although is populated upon each plugin's PreFilter invocation, is not injected into `CycleState` when some PreFilter returns unschedulable:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2c6c4566eff972d6c1320b5f8ad795f88c822d09/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L655-L661

So think about this workflow:

- pluginA returns Skip in its PreFilter
- pluginB return Unschedulable in its PreFilter
- note: pluginA is not included in `CycleState.SkipFilterPlugins` due to aforementioned bug
- a Pod is claimed as unschedulable (failed by pluginB)
- during PostFilter, it's **supposed** to bypass pluginA's PreEnqueueExtension's AddPod/RemovePod, but it doesn't
- calling a "skipped" Plugin's AddPod/RemovePod during preemption, sometimes will abort the whole preemption as the logic tries to read info from cycleState, and some plugin's "skip" version doesn't fill cycleState properly, e.g., InterPodAffinity (skip immediately w/o write preFilterStateKey).

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2c6c4566eff972d6c1320b5f8ad795f88c822d09/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/interpodaffinity/filtering.go#L257-L262

### What did you expect to happen?

Short circuiting using Skip is fine, but `CycleState.SkipFilterPlugins` should injected properly at all cases.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Described in the workflow above.

It's firstly captured in an out-of-tree PostFilter plugin: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/scheduler-plugins/pull/608#issuecomment-1665855370, but can also happen in in-tree plugins.

### Anything else we need to know

title: the preemption happens even when PreFilter returns UnschedulableAndUnresolvable
body:
When PreFilter returns UnschedulableAndUnresolvable, we don't need to run the preemption, but currently we run.
This unexpected preemption could cause errors from the preemption by trying to read non-exist PreFilter data.

As @Huang-Wei pointed out ([ref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119770#issuecomment-1666418637)), actually we didn't run the preemption in such cases in the past versions, but https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/110894 introduced this bug.

/kind bug 
/kind regression
/sig scheduling
/triage accepted
/priority important-soon

title: Kube-apiserver high memory usage on pending pods storm
body:
**What happened**:
The kube-apiserver consumed memory spiked to ~90G the moment we upscaled the cluster with +400 nodes while having thousands of pending pods.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2542264/105851679-1722a880-5fec-11eb-9517-081e77c029a2.png)
This resulted in OOM kill of the kube-apiserver pods causing outage. Example:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2542264/105851827-43d6c000-5fec-11eb-8d36-3ec6b92c8365.png)

**What you expected to happen**:
The kube-apiserver should not consume that much memory resulting in OOM. I understand that under the presented conditions there could be performance penalties on kube-apiserver or kube-scheduler delaying the pods' startup, but it should not lead to OOM kill.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
1. Have a deployment with pods requesting for 4CPU and 4G MEM
2. Scale the deployment to a huge number of replicas: 2000
3. Prevent the CA to autoscale the cluster (i.e. uninstall the cluster-autoscaler/scale it to 0 replicas)
4. Wait for ~30min-1h (there is no pattern here, it could happen even faster)
5. Manually scale the cluster out to 400 nodes
6. Monitor the kube-apiserver MEM usage

**Anything else we need to know?**:
This in conjunction with cilium and contour+envoy could lead to ingress failures.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
```
$ kubectl version
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"16", GitVersion:"v1.16.2", GitCommit:"c97fe5036ef3df2967d086711e6c0c405941e14b", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2019-10-15T23:41:55Z", GoVersion:"go1.12.10", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"darwin/amd64"}

### What happened?

Adding `"containerLogMaxSize": "100Mi"` to kubelet-config had no effect. 
The containerLogMaxSize remained at 10Mi.

On the other hand, adding ` --container-log-max-size="100Mi"` to the command line produced a warning in the log file, but did seem to work:

Flag --container-log-max-size has been deprecated, This parameter should be set via the config file specified by the Kubelet's --config flag. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/kubelet-config-file/ for more information.
```

### What did you expect to happen?

Either adding adding `"containerLogMaxSize": "100Mi"` to kubelet-config would actually set the container max size, or there would be no deprecation warning when using the CLI option.


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Use eksctl to create a minimal EKS cluster.
2. ssh into one of the worker nodes.
3. Edit the file `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet/kubelet-config.json` to include the following line:
```
  "containerLogMaxSize": "100Mi"
```
4. Run the following
```
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl restart containerd
systemctl restart kubelet

journalctl -u kubelet | grep FLAG | grep container-log-max

FLAG: --container-log-max-size="10Mi"

title: VolumeZone scheduling plugin should handle csi migration
body:
### What happened?

In https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114268, we discovered that our plan for eventually removing the [VolumeZone](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/volumezone) scheduling plugin when CSI migration is GA is not possible because the plugin also applies to non-migratable volume types.

However, if we leave the plugin as is, then even migratable PVs will be broken if we remove beta topology labels from Nodes in the future. This is because the plugin does not have any handling for migrated volumes.


### What did you expect to happen?

I suggest we add CSI migration handling to the VolumeZone plugin. I think we just need to detect if the volume is migrated, and if so, skip the VolumeZone processing. For migrated volumes, we translate `PV.Labels` into `PV.NodeAffinity` so they end up getting processed by the [VolumeBinding](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/volumebinding) plugin.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

In a cluster with csi migration for a specific intree volume type enabled,
1. create an intree PV with beta topology labels
2. remove the beta topology label from a node
3. try to schedule a pod using that pv

title: kubelet client cert is not getting auto-rotated (K8s 1.21)
body:
### What happened?

Deployed Kubernetes on a single node setup (master+worker). The setup was UP, checked Kubelet + certs managed by Kubeadm has a validity of 1yr. Now, changed the date of the system to 30% of the cert's expiry date. 

Ran Kubeadm certs renew all, certs managed by Kubeadm got renewed from the day to the next year on the same date. 
but Kubelet client cert "/var/lib/kubelet/pki" is not auto-rotated still pointing to old certificate. 

Waited for 1day, still didn't get rotate. 

**As mentioned in the k8s official document**
As the expiration of the signed certificate approaches, the kubelet will automatically issue a new certificate signing request, using the Kubernetes API. This can happen at any point **between 30% and 10%**f the time remaining on the certificate. Again, the controller manager will automatically approve the certificate request and attach a signed certificate to the certificate signing request. The kubelet will retrieve the new signed certificate from the Kubernetes API and write that to disk. Then it will update the connections it has to the Kubernetes API to reconnect using the new certificate.



Also tried below setup to manually generate or rotate client certificate.

Call 'kubeadm init phase kubeconfig kubelet' optionally pass -config or other flags if needed. This will generate kubelet.conf with embedded cert and key.
Restart kubelet and wait for it to generate new certs in /var/lib/kubelet/pki
Call 'kubeadm init phase kubelet-finalize all'. This will 'symlink' the kebelet.conf to kubelet cert rotation.
Restart kubelet again.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/102556

new certs didn't get generate. 


### What did you expect to happen?

Kubelet certs should get auto-rotate. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Deploy k8s, and change the date to 30% of the expiry date of the certificate. and wait for kubelet to auto-rotate the client certificate.

title: Kubelet creates leases without ownerReference set if node doesn't exist
body:
### What happened?

* Some external controller deleted node object while kubelet was alive
* Due to ignoring errors in kubelet's lease logic, it created lease without ownerReference set

### What did you expect to happen?

* Kubelet doesn't create lease without ownerReference set in any case, even pathological one

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

* Some external controller deletes node object
* Garbage collector properly deletes associated lease object
* Kubelet tries to update object and it fails on Conflict (saying that UID doesn't match): 
  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b1e130fe83156783153538b6d79821c2fdaa85bb/staging/src/k8s.io/component-helpers/apimachinery/lease/controller.go#L179-L198
* We go to `apierrors.IsConflict(err)` branch, call backoffEnsureLease and assign result to base, but backoffEnsureLease may return potentially invalid object if ensureLease returned error (which happens when newLeasePostProcessFunc returns error, e.g. when node doesn't exist).
* We `continue`
* The next loop calls c.newLease on the incorrect base and ignores error in line 181 (so the second attempt to call newLeasePostProcessFunc which also fails with an error) 
* We do UPDATE with incomplete (without effect of newLeasePostProcessFunc) object
* Given that leases allow CreateOnUpdate a new object, without ownerReference is created: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b1e130fe83156783153538b6d79821c2fdaa85bb/pkg/registry/coordination/lease/strategy.go#L65-L68

title: API: ResourceRequirements usage in Container and PVC
body:
### What happened?

The same ResourceRequirements struct is used in two only loosely related entities (Container and PersistentVolumeClaim). Extending ResourceRequirements for dynamic resource requirement had the unintended effect that the new `Claims` field also became available in a PersistentVolumeClaim.



### What did you expect to happen?

Extending one should not affect the other.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/111023#pullrequestreview-1302112278:

> We just ran across this while reviewing https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/107776
>
> The ResourceRequirements type is also used within the PersistentVolumeSpec type (which is also used indirectly in pod specs via ephemeral volumes), and the "clear if feature-gate is disabled" logic is only wired to podspec-handling. That means in 1.26 PVC objects or PodSpecs with ephemeral volumes defined can persist data in this field even if the feature is disabled.
>
> Can you open a PR to clear this field in PVC and ephemeral volume create/update flows, and file a follow-up issue to consider splitting the type used in PVCs so it doesn't continue inheriting work done that is targeted at pods?

### What happened?

A client is allowed to add custom finalizers to Custom Resources with a finalizer name that's not fully qualified (e.g. `example` or `example.com`).

However they're prevented from doing the same on builtin resource types, returning the following error:

    Invalid value: "finalizers.compute.linkedin.com": name is neither a standard finalizer name nor is it fully qualified

### What did you expect to happen?

Per [Custom Resource Definition docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/extend-kubernetes/custom-resources/custom-resource-definitions/#finalizers:~:text=Identifiers%20of%20custom%20finalizers%20consist%20of%20a%20domain%20name%2C%20a%20forward%20slash%20and%20the%20name%20of%20the%20finalizer), custom finalizer names are expected to be in format "consist of a domain name, a forward slash and the name of the finalizer" (e.g. `foo.bar/name`).

Therefore, I expected the enforcement to be the same for CRs and builtin types.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. have a custom resource on the cluster
2. `kubectl edit` it to add `finalizers: [example.com]`
3. observe the edit does not fail
4. do the same on a builtin resource (e.g. Namespace or Pod), observe it fails

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

Reproducible at least starting from 1.21 and still on latest versions.

title: dynamic-resource-allocation: Issue with changes introduced in #114844 to add a timeout to kubelet calls to plugins
body:
Issue with changes introduced in #114844 to add a timeout to kubelet calls made to DRA plugins

When my plugin takes longer than 10 seconds to respond, the `NodePrepareResource()` call in the client (presumably) fails, but the failure is never bubbled up to the manager. Later on a timeout happens somewhere else in the stack (after 90s) and a *new* call to `NodePrepareResource()` in the manager is issued. This one succeeds (because my call only takes a very short amount of time because it returns a cached allocation from the first call). The first call *never* returns though, presumably blocked somewhere down inside the client.

To verify this, I temporarily extended the timeout beyond the length of time it takes for my plugin to succeed and everything works as expected.

/cc @bart0sh

_Originally posted by @klueska in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114844#issuecomment-1499353458_

title: fix KUBE-MARK-MASQ ownership (kubelet vs kube-proxy)
body:
The `KUBE-MARK-MASQ` and `KUBE-POSTROUTING` chains are currently created by both kubelet and kube-proxy. There have long been comments in the code suggesting that they should be managed only by kubelet, and we should do that.

History:
  - Marking packets to be masqueraded later first appeared in kube-proxy in #12764.
  - #20496 introduced the modern `KUBE-MARK-MASQ` / `KUBE-POSTROUTING` (set up from `pkg/proxy/iptables`)
  - #25604 added `HostPort` support to kubenet, making use of the proxier's `KUBE-MARK-MASQ` chain but adding a comment to the proxier noting that kubelet should be creating that chain and the proxy should just assume that it exists.
  - #30486 required the addition of the `KUBE-MARK-DROP` chain, and was used as an opportunity to start moving `KUBE-MARK-MASQ` to kubelet. But the code to create the chain was not removed from the proxier, so now kubelet and kube-proxy both create it. (But only kubelet creates `KUBE-MARK-DROP`.) A comment was included in the kubelet code: `TODO: clean up this logic in kube-proxy`.
  - #46580 added `pkg/proxy/ipvs`, which copied a lot of iptables code and so now also creates `KUBE-MARK-MASQ` itself (and depends on kubelet creating `KUBE-MARK-DROP`).

### What would you like to be added?

kubedrain has "onPodDeletedOrEvicted" callback that can be used in custom controllers. It would be very helpful if we add more callbacks that can give more granular control over monitoring, like "onPodDeletionOrEvicitionStarted" and "onPodDeletionOrEvictionFailed".

title: CronJob gets stuck when jobs quota is reached
body:
### What happened?

We (in Booking.com) run CronJobs in Kubernetes clusters with ResourceQuota's defined. When quota for # of jobs is reached we observed that CronJobs:
1. stop scheduling new jobs (because quota is reached),
2. don't clean the old jobs (despite # of jobs > history allows and the fact that it would unblock the CronJob new Jobs). 

The only way to progress is to remove enough Jobs to make room for a new Job in namespace quota. When we do that manually, the CronJob kicks in.

The workaround we found around the internet is to specify `ttlSecondsAfterFinished` for the job template. But it's not ideal as it's not a history-based limit, but a time-based limit, and often you want to have the last N jobs to be around for debugging.

### What did you expect to happen?

When jobs quota is reached and # of cronjob jobs exceeds specified the history limit, these jobs are deleted giving room for new jobs to run.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```yaml
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: job-quota
  namespace: default
spec:
  hard:
    count/jobs.batch: "1"
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: hello-world-cronjob
spec:
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 0
  schedule: "* * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
            - name: hello-world
              image: bash
              command: ["bash", "-c", "sleep 80"]
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

1. Wait for a first Job to be created (which will fill up the jobs quota) at X minute.
2. A job for X + 1 will fail to be created (because quota won't allow, and X job is still running).
3. All future attempts to create a new job by the controller will fail (check `kubectl get events --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail`, you'll see re-occuring `Error creating job: jobs.batch "hello-world-cronjob-28187648" is forbidden: exceeded quota: job-quota, requested: cou

title: kube-apiserver doesn't clean up OpenAPI properly after deleting an APIService/CRD
body:
### What happened?

I noticed some odd behaviors/logs after deleting APIServices and CRDs.

First, only CRDs were removed from the response of `/openapi/v3` and APIServices were not removed. Not only the root path, the APIService's specific paths were also available, e.g. `/openapi/v3/apis/foo.bar.com/v1alpha1`, as if they were not deleted.

Second, there were some confusing logs in kube-apiserver, indicating it failed to do some cleanup, and every failure was duplicated once:
```
E0822 15:24:36.314675       1 controller.go:159] removing "v1alpha1.crd.antrea.io" from AggregationController failed with: resource not found
E0822 15:24:36.314705       1 controller.go:159] removing "v1alpha1.crd.antrea.io" from AggregationController failed with: resource not found
E0822 15:24:36.316316       1 controller.go:159] removing "v1beta1.crd.antrea.io" from AggregationController failed with: resource not found
E0822 15:24:36.317664       1 controller.go:159] removing "v1beta1.crd.antrea.io" from AggregationController failed with: resource not found
```

After checking the code, I found the above observations were caused by the same code in kube-apiserver which didn't handle the removal of APIService correctly:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/aa8cb97f65fe1d24e96eda129337d86109615570/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/apiserver/apiserver.go#L563-L568

Basically apiserver was calling wrong AggregationController when removing APIService, which caused OpenAPI v3 not cleaned up and the duplicate errors. There was another issue in v2 AggregationController which caused the error. 

Besides, just correcting L567 didn't fix the problem totally, there were some other issues in the implementation.

### What did you expect to happen?

kube-apiserver should clean up OpenAPI correctly, shoud not generate confusing errors.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Install some APIServices and CRDs and remove all of them,

title: Conntrack cleaning happens before network programming endpoints
body:
### What happened?

Currently kube-proxy efficiently cleans all stale conntrack entries preventing traffic black holing for deleted endpoints, but there can be some corner cases when conntrack cleaning happens before programming the network leaving a small window in which if any packet arrives will back-hole the traffic.

The corner case:
Taking a simple case of load-balancer service backed by a deployment with single replica, on deleting the pod(gracefully), I observed two **OnEndpointSliceUpdate** invocations:
1.  First one with EndpointConditions.Ready as false
2. EndpointSlice was cleared for the pod 

The conntrack flow for this case:
1. After processing the first **OnEndpointSliceUpdate** invocation **EndpointsMap** will still have entries for the pod as endpoint still exists, though not in ready state so proxier won't program deletion of endpoint from the data path. But the endpoint IP will be picked for conntrack cleaning as new endpoint != old endpoint because of the not ready condition.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/95e915c4288eda15da1724989f3f7dec9f3512d6/pkg/proxy/endpoints.go#L423-L436
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/95e915c4288eda15da1724989f3f7dec9f3512d6/pkg/proxy/endpoints.go#L120-L126

2.  After processing the second **OnEndpointSliceUpdate** invocation **EndpointsMap** won't have entries for the endpoint and the proxier will program deletion of the endpoint in the data path. EndpointIP won't be picked up for conntrack cleaning as the following logic will skip it
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/95e915c4288eda15da1724989f3f7dec9f3512d6/pkg/proxy/endpoints.go#L417-L421

This behaviour leads to conntrack cleaning one cycle ahead of network programming.  
This might be a regression of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/106163

### What did you expect to happen?

Conntrack cleanup should happen after programming the network.

title: "Connection reset by peer" due to invalid conntrack packets
body:
### What happened?

When packets with sequence number out-of-window arrived k8s node, conntrack marked them as INVALID. kube-proxy will ignore them, without rewriting DNAT. However, there is no corresponding session link on the host, and the host sends a reset packet, causing the session link to be interrupted

### What did you expect to happen?

connection not reset

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/74839

### Anything else we need to know?

This problem can be solved by command：
iptables -t filter -I INPUT -p tcp -m conntrack --ctstate INVALID -j DROP

Similar issue:https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/74839
But this issue "drop" is placed on the forward chain, our scenario needs to be placed on the input chain.

### Kubernetes version

title: kube-proxy: Drop packets in INVALID state drops packets from outside the pod range
body:
**What happened**:
When kube-proxy is configured with a cluster-cidr range, it drops packets with an INVALID conntrack state for all sources on the KUBE-FORWARD chain. This is meant to prevent spurious retransmits in long-lived TCP connections to a service IP, but it prevents clusters from having asymmetrical routing on private subnets with services outside of a cluster. 

**What you expected to happen**:
Packets on the KUBE-FORWARD chain with an INVALID conntrack state should be dropped for only sources inside of the cluster-cidr if set.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
N/A

**Anything else we need to know?**:
Change to drop INVALID conntrack packets was in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/74840. Backing out that commit and compiling is my current workaround.

title: Enhance discoverability of user-installed plugins
body:
### What would you like to be added?


Extend the kubectl help output with a dynamic section on user-installed plugins, e.g.:

```
User-Installed Plugin Commands:
  convert       The command convert is a plugin installed by the user
  krew          The command krew is a plugin installed by the user
```

### Why is this needed?

Right now, the output of `kubectl` and `kubectl` help is static and does not include dynamic-inclusion of user-installed plugins.

This is inconsistent with the behavior of the auto-completion options, e.g. `kubectl kr<tab>` exposes `kubectl krew` as possible command, while it is omitted by `kubectl` and `kubectl help` (given that the krew plugin manager for kubectl is installed)

title: Kubernetes api returns incorrect conflicting fields during server-side apply in some cases
body:
### What happened?

When performing a server-side apply PATCH request, if there are conflicts in what's being applied with differing field owners, kubernetes responds with a 409 conflict error with an array of causes in the error detail, enumerating the conflicting fields that were discovered.

In some cases, we see that the fields returned in this 409 error response are incorrect, containing both duplicate fields, and entirely missing other conflicts.

### What did you expect to happen?

The http 409 error response when receiving a conflict while using server-side apply should contain all of the correct fields (and also ideally no duplicates).

title: Cloud provider implementations do not show provider-specific options in usage string
body:
### What happened?

The `NewCloudControllerManagerCommand` function in `k8s.io/cloud-provider/app/controllermanager.go` accepts an `additionalFlags` parameter which it describes as a way to "controller specific flags to be included in the complete set of controller manager flags". However, when the usage string is shown (either via `$cmd --help` or when parsing options fails), these additional options are not included in the usage string.	

This was identified via code inspection while trying to figure out what options did in `openstack-cloud-controller-manager`.

### What did you expect to happen?

For e.g. `aws-cloud-controller-manager`, the output of `aws-cloud-controller-manager --help` should include a `Tagging Controller Options` section corresponding to [the flagset registered for that command](https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider-aws/blob/v1.28.1/cmd/aws-cloud-controller-manager/main.go#L67-L83). This section should in turn list all of [the options added to that flagset](https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider-aws/blob/v1.28.1/pkg/controllers/options/tagging_controller.go#L30-L38).

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Build a cloud provider executable that includes additional options, such as `aws-cloud-controller-manager`
2. Run `$cmd --help`
3. Observe the additional options are not shown in the output

title: Node Graceful Shutdown is taking too long
body:
### What happened?

Pods usually have a 30s grace period when they do not define a terminationGracePeriodSeconds for termination. When NodeGraceful Shutdown is enabled the grace period gets set to the ShutdownGracePeriodSeconds, which is configured by the Kubelet. Let's say the Kubelet is configured with a ShutdownGracePeriodSeconds of 65 minutes. This means that pods without a termination grace period can terminate with a grace period of 65 minutes.

The Kubelet configuration includes:

```
...
shutdownGracePeriod: 65m
shutdownGracePeriodCriticalPods: 35m
```

alternatively, this alternate configuration does not work either:
```
...
shutdownGracePeriodByPodPriority:
  - priority: 0
    shutdownGracePeriodSeconds: 300
  - priority: 10000
    shutdownGracePeriodSeconds: 600
  - priority: 2000000000
    shutdownGracePeriodSeconds: 1200
  - priority: 2000001000
    shutdownGracePeriodSeconds: 1200
```

The Kubernetes E2E tests timeout when this configuration is applied as the default, since many E2E tests and pods do not set a terminationGracePeriodSeconds field.

The fix is to set the [graceful termination](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dd6bc2548e008e5d49a62dff73af1aa18712a1cb/pkg/kubelet/nodeshutdown/nodeshutdown_manager_linux.go#L368C1-L368C1) to 30 seconds by default, and allow the shutdown code to override the [grace period](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dd6bc2548e008e5d49a62dff73af1aa18712a1cb/pkg/kubelet/nodeshutdown/nodeshutdown_manager_linux.go#L372) if the pod sets one.

### What did you expect to happen?

I expect pods without a terminationGracePeriodSeconds to be terminated after 30 seconds with a large `shutdownGracePeriod` set within Kubelet.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Configure Kubelet with this config:

```
...
shutdownGracePeriod: 65m
shutdownGracePeriodCriticalPods: 35m
```

Create a pod without a terminationGracePeriodSeconds and o

title: kubectl drain error message confusing when using with operator
body:
/kind bug

**What happened**:
Scenario:
- You run an etcd cluster with etcd-operator
- You drain a node with etcd-operator on it.

You get a message like:
```
$ kubectl drain $NODE
pods not managed by ReplicationController, ReplicaSet, Job, DaemonSet or StatefulSet (use --force to override): example-etcd-cluster-0002
```
This error message is not useful, given that Operators are popular and recommended.

**What you expected to happen**:
No error message.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
```
# PREREQ: have a Cluster.  

# Install coreos operator as follows:
mkdir coreos
cd coreos
git clone https://github.com/coreos/etcd-operator
cd etcd-operator/
example/rbac/create_role.sh
kubectl create -f example/deployment.yaml
kubectl get customresourcedefinitions

# Make an etcd cluster
kubectl create -f example/example-etcd-cluster.yaml
kubectl get pods -L etcd_cluster -l etcd_cluster=example-etcd-cluster
kubectl get etcdcluster example-etcd-cluster -o json | jq .status.members
# Wait until some guys are ready
watch "kubectl get etcdcluster example-etcd-cluster -o json | jq .status.members"

# Find a node that has an etcd pod on it. Call it $NODE.
# in example, NODE="gke-cluster-2-default-pool-4904abf8-mt8t"

title: Transient Driver Registration on the CSINode can Result in Missed NodeUnstageVolume RPCs During Pod Migration
body:
### What happened?

In `unmountDetachDevices` (see [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconciler_common.go#L279-L316)) we have the following code that will ultimately dispatch `NodeUnstageVolume` RPCs to the underlying CSI plugin.

Here is a pseudo-code representation of the current logic:

```
function unmountDetachDevices
	for all unmounted volumes in ASoW
		if volume not in DSoW &&
		   not operation pending on volume
			if device is mounted globally or
			   device is mounted uncertain
				Case A:
				unmount device
				(this will kick off the NodeUnstageVolume RPC; we want to be here)
			else
				Case B:
				just remove volume from ASoW
				(general badness since we don't issue a NodeUnstageVolume RPC)
```

In our testbeds, we have observed a number of occurrences where we fall into `Case B` when the CSI Node plugin for a particular driver is being bounced, which leads to the volumemanager failing to dispatch the `NodeUnstageVolume` RPC. If the pod migrates to another node, this will leave behind a Zombie LUN in our testbeds (we're using iSCSI).

A Zombie LUN can and often does result in corruption when other pods later migrate to the node in question.

Based on testing that we conducted, we discovered that this case occurs because the device is marked as unmounted.

Initially, we see the device marked as uncertain during reconstruction.

However, if the CSI Node driver pod is bounced in the exact window when a `NodeStageVolume` RPC is issued, then we end up [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L777C1-L798C2).

There we check to see if the error encountered is a “transient error” or a “final error”; if a “final error” is encountered, then the device state transitions from uncertain to unmounted. That is what is happening in our case.

The error is generated when the CSIClient ca

title: Endpoint / Endpointslice objects become stuck in state where IP condition differs (not ready vs ready)
body:
### What happened?

We recently upgraded kubernetes from 1.20.12 to 1.24.10 . We now periodically experience an issue where services will "disconnect" from their endpoint, even though there were no changes to the status of the pod it references, or the node the pod is on. The issue can occur with one or more services and it always starts at the same time for all services it affects. Usually all these services have the same selector. However, it doesn't always affect all the services with that selector. For example, we could have 5 services with the same selector and only 3 of them stop working.

After this "disconnect", the endpoint object for the service shows the pod ip in NotReadyAddresses while the endpointslice object shows the ip with condition being ready. **It gets stuck in this state until we either delete the pod or endpoint or restart controller manager.**

I'm trying to understand whether a behaviour we are observing in stateful sets with `Parallel` `PodManagementPolicy` is expected or if we are hitting a bug.

> Parallel pod management tells the StatefulSet controller to launch or terminate all Pods in parallel, and to not wait for Pods to become Running and Ready or completely terminated prior to launching or terminating another Pod. I'm trying to understand the last bit "Updates are not affected". Unless I am misunderstanding the intention here, we expect that during scale up and down pods will be created and terminated in parallel. title: Make UDP timeouts set via kube-proxy config (for ipvs mode) also change timeouts in Conntrack
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Make UDP timeouts set via kube-proxy config (for ipvs mode) also change timeouts in Conntrack, just like it already works for TCP.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120076#issuecomment-1693548013

### Why is this needed?

For settings consistency: current behavior for setting TCP timeouts is superior compared to setting UDP timeouts for no good reason. As a consequence, one has to manually modify `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_udp_timeout`/`nf_conntrack_udp_timeout_stream` on the underlying nodes OSes.

title: [FR]: implement fsUser option for securityContext
body:
Hello,

currently, it seems not to be possible to project secrets or configmaps to files with strict permissions to containers.

Some applications such as `sshd` require strict permissions on some files like `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`, mainly, it requires that this file is owned by the user. For the `sshd` there is an option to bypass this restriction `StrictModes`. However, there are different like `psql` that is able to use `~/.pgpass` only with the correct permissions. Operators like cloudnative-pg create a secret that could be projected to `~/.pgpass`, but owner cannot be set thus `psql` refuses to use it.

I think it would be great, if `fsUser` option could be implemented or some other option that could be used to specify the owner of projected secrets/configmaps.

title: [FR] External network egress selector.
body:
Currently, the [egress network selection logic](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/util/webhook/authentication.go#L67) always uses the cluster network when the webhook is specified by service, and always uses the control plane network when the webhook is specified by [url](https://github.com/kubernetes/api/blob/master/admissionregistration/v1/types.go#L530).

This can cause problems with webhooks that are hosted externally to the cluster & control plane. For example, suppose for security reasons you want to only allow egress to a very limited set of host:ports in the control plane network.

There are a couple options for how this could work:
- Single `External` network type vs. arbitrary number of "named" networks
- Opt-in to external network vs. opt in to control plane network (by CIDR?)
- How should DNS names be handled?

/sig api-machinery
/kind feature

title: Garbage collector for container images is unpredictable and inconsistent
body:
### What happened?

The garbage collector for container image lifecycle does not seem to adhere to the documentation and the provided parameters.

From [the docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/architecture/garbage-collection/#container-image-lifecycle), _the configured HighThresholdPercent value triggers garbage collection, which deletes images in order based on the last time they were used, starting with the oldest first. The kubelet deletes images until disk usage reaches the LowThresholdPercent value._

From some tests, this does not appear to be the case. Often, the GC will delete way more images than requires, often dropping below `LowThresholdPercent` and deleting 3 to 4 at a time.

### What did you expect to happen?

The GC should delete images until `LowThresholdPercent` is reached.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Either create some dummy images (we created a set of images with increasing sizes, but any will do the job), or identify some appropriate image already available on Docker Hub.
2. For each image, deploy a pod and then delete it. The image will remain in the cache.
3. After a while, the disk space will reach the `LowThresholdPercent` first and `HighThresholdPercent` later. The GC will be triggered.
4. The GC should in theory delete the earliest unused image. This does not always happen: priority is sometimes given to other images, or more than one is deleted, in a seemingly random order.

### Anything else we need to know?

The bug is hard to reproduce and needs some trial and error. Sometimes, images are correctly deleted in order and one at a time, other times the behaviour is apparently random.

If this behaviour is expected, then the docs should be appropriately corrected to mention the choices the GC makes. This is important as I/O spikes in the GC may cause SLA issues in other services deployed in the node.

title: Updating pods during scheduling may produce dirty data
body:
### What happened?

If we update a pod（such as update annotation） during the scheduling process, the scheduler's podInformer will generate an update event. If the pod has not been assumed at this time, this event will be added to the scheduling queue. When the pod is scheduled succeed, since the pod is still in the scheduling queue, the pod may be scheduled again. 

If there are many pods in the scheduling queue, the pod cannot be scheduled until 30 seconds later. At this time, the pod information in assumedPods has been cleared, and the pod will be scheduled again. Since the pod has been scheduled succeed, this scheduling will fail, and the scheduler will continue to retry, repeating the cycle. This pod will always become dirty data in the scheduler unless the scheduler is restarted.


### What did you expect to happen?

If the pod has been scheduled succeed, the scheduler should not schedule dirty data in the queue.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a pod；
2. When the pod starts scheduling, update the pod before assume（This step can be achieved by adding breakpoints through local debugging）；
3. After the update event generated by the pod enters the scheduling queue, we should guaranteed the pod  to be scheduled again after 30 seconds（Implemented through local breakpoint debugging）；
4. The pod has been scheduled, but the scheduler is still scheduling the pod in a loop.

### Anything else we need to know?

title: When deleting pods on the same node in batches, the exited container may remain, causing pod records to remain.
body:
### What happened?

During performance testing, I found that when deleting pods on a node in batches, such as 100, the problem of pod deletion failure may occur. The exited container may remain, causing pod records to remain. I think this problem is related to the implementation of pod_container_deletor.go that containerDeletorBufferLimit is only 50. and in the func (p *podContainerDeletor) deleteContainersInPod, when the worker channel is full, it discards the event. I think using work queue instead of channel is a better solution. And the processing logic of runtime.DeleteContainer needs to be optimized. The processing can be skipped for containers that have been externally deleted or cannot be found. 

And i found it still almost the same solution in podContainerDeletor. The master branch may also have the same problem.

I will submit a PR later for this issue.



### What did you expect to happen?

pods and containers can be deleted successfully

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

batch delete over than 100 pods that on same node

title: External service UDP fails while TCP works due to definition processing asymmetry
body:
### What happened?

I have a single node k3s installation. I'd like to use it as an entry point even if some services are installed on separate VMs, not on K8s. External services work nicely when the service is available via TCP, but not when it's UDP as the system thinks UDP service doesn't have Endpoint definition and creates deny rules for iptables. The YAML is symmetric to the TCP one.

Working TCP:
````
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: bugreport-works
  namespace: mate
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  ports:
  - port: 4321
    name: works-tcp
    protocol: TCP
    targetPort: 4321
---
kind: Endpoints
apiVersion: v1
metadata:
  name: bugreport-works
  namespace: mate
subsets:
  - addresses:
      - ip: 192.168.122.108
    ports:
      - port: 4321
        name: works-tcp
````

Not working UDP:
````
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: bugreport-fails
  namespace: mate
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  ports:
  - port: 4321
    name: fails-udp
    protocol: UDP
    targetPort: 4321
---
kind: Endpoints
apiVersion: v1
metadata:
  name: bugreport-fails
  namespace: mate
subsets:
  - addresses:
      - ip: 192.168.122.108
    ports:
      - port: 4321
        name: fails-udp
````

For UDP I see these generated rejection rules (for TCP, there is no any similar):
```
-A KUBE-EXTERNAL-SERVICES -d 192.168.31.133/32 -p udp -m comment --comment "mate/bugreport-fails:fails-udp has no endpoints" -m udp --dport 4321 -j REJECT --reject-with icmp-port-unreachable
-A KUBE-EXTERNAL-SERVICES -p udp -m comment --comment "mate/bugreport-fails:fails-udp has no endpoints" -m addrtype --dst-type LOCAL -m udp --dport 31974 -j REJECT --reject-with icmp-port-unreachable
-A KUBE-SERVICES -d 10.43.215.148/32 -p udp -m comment --comment "mate/bugreport-fails:fails-udp has no endpoints" -m udp --dport 4321 -j REJECT --reject-with icmp-port-unreachable
```

### What did you expect to happen?

TCP and UDP definitions

title: [1.28.2] Keeps zfs pool busy on UnmountVolume via csi-provider
body:
### What happened?

We are running our custom csi provider to mount zfs via iscsi, this is operating since at least 1.20 and never showed any issues.

It does not implement the NodeStage / NodeUnstage apis, and only uses the NodePublishVolume / NodeUnpublishVolume.

Since upgrading to 1.28.2 the Unmount progress gets stuck and the zfs pool keeps busy indefinitely.

A solution to fix the stuck pool is to delete the folder of the pv inside of the pod, this leads to log spam by kubelet it can't find the corresponding .json file for the csi provider, and a restart of kubelet afterwards allows the pool to be actually exported.

### What did you expect to happen?

Do not keep the mounted volume busy when Unmounting via CSI providers.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Possibly other providers also see those issues?

### Anything else we need to know?

Kubelet logs the following, whereas the message is passed from the csi plugin:

```

title: Network readiness for indexed job + headless service depends on presence of pod
body:
### What happened?

I work on an operator that creates an Indexed Job alongside a headless service to give the indexed job pods a shared network. We used to have a design where we would create a one-off pod before the indexed job to generate a certificate, and recently refactored to have the library built into the operator, and remove the need for the pod. The unexpected consequence of this is that (within the indexed job, where a broker is starting and connecting to the workers with zeromq) we started to see huge delay times in this happening - jobs that took 11-12 seconds previously now would take 40 and upwards to 140. We were able to debug and determine that the different was that the network wasn't ready by the time the broker came up, so zeromq had a timeout (with exponential backoff) that was kicking in, and this explained the _huge_ wait times. We were able to define a parameter within our broker that would hard code the timeout to be smaller, and get the times back down to something reasonable (closer to 20-30) but this doesn't explain the fact that the network still wasn't ready after this change.

I did some testing - namely bringing up a one-off service pod (nginx, although largely it doesn't seem to matter what it does) and consistently with the service pod the network is always ready for the broker. You can see those results here:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/814322/236543136-1e825cc8-f5e0-4df8-b015-811be4a1b890.png)

And specifically, note how the green (having the service) is consistently much faster than the purple (no service) with the exception of 8 seconds - I'm not sure what happened there! Also note the last column - when no timeout is set, zeromq does it's default thing and then exponential backoff kicks off and you are waiting quite a long time for a very small job to run. title: Split etcd /health endpoint to /livez and /readyz
body:
### What would you like to be added?

k/k tracking issue for https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/issues/16007

etcd currently has a single health endpoint for etcd /health which is used in Kubernetes distros as both liveness and readiness checking. In order to be fully api-compliant, etcd should have both a liveness check (i.e. /livez) which checks that this individual etcd member is "alive" and does not need to be restarted and a readiness check (i.e. /readyz) which signals that the etcd member is ready to accept traffic.

We are seeking feedbacks for the plan and we also need to change the default etcd health check configs in kubeadm after that is done. 

### Why is this needed?

We are trying to make etcd fully api-compliant.

title: `poststarthook/apiservice-registration-controller` check blocks apiserver readiness for 1 minute if discovery cannot be completed
body:
### What happened?

I’m seeing some odd behavior with 1.28.2 that was not present in earlier releases, with regards to aggregated api services. It appears that the `poststarthook/apiservice-registration-controller` is now blocking the apiserver from becoming ready for 1 minute, if discovery for an aggregated apiservice is not available when the apiserver is started. Note that this only happens if the apiservice is marked available when the apiserver is started; if it is unavailable at startup (Available status: false), or the service has no endpoints, the health check does not block and readyz returns `ok` without delay.

I am seeing this behavior in 1.28.1 and 1.28.2, but not v1.27.6 or v1.27.5

### What did you expect to happen?

apiserver becomes ready without any additional delays

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Deploy metrics-server to a Kubernetes cluster
2. Wait for api registration for `v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io` to complete (Available status is `true`).
3. Kill the kubelet and pods on the node hosting the metrics-server pod, such that the metrics-server service continues to show available endpoints, but the endpoint is not reachable.
4. Restart the apiserver before the `v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io` apiservice is marked unavailable
5. Note that the `poststarthook/apiservice-registration-controller` check blocks readiness for 1 minute. After 1 minute the Available status is updated to `false`, and the health check passes.

title: kubelet: lookup node address logic for external provider assign wrong PodIPs to hostNetwork pods
body:
The kubelet  logic used to get the Node addresses when using an external provider, temporary assigns an address discovered from the node , this address can be overriden later by the external cloud provider

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0241da314e0e69817d66313b45a69c19d1ce7327/pkg/kubelet/nodestatus/setters.go#L123-L131


This was implemented in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/75229 to improve the  bootstrapping problems with some external cloud providers

The side effect of this behavior is that if the external cloud provider sets a different address/es, then the pods with `HostNetwork: true` will be showing the "first" addresses as their `PodIPs`, since we don't mutate those IPs once set to avoid problems

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0241da314e0e69817d66313b45a69c19d1ce7327/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L1770-L1786

I think that we should revert the existing logic for external cloud providers, since is causing a temporary and inconsistent state and it seem to address mainly a problem with kubeadm https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/75229#issuecomment-516592142 but kubeadm folks seems to not need this functionality https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/75229#issuecomment-516580449


/kind bug
/sig network
/sig node

title: Pods are stuck ContainerCreating after volume detach error and KCM restart
body:
### What happened?

After KCM restart, any Pod that reuses a volume that failed to detach gets stuck ContainerCreating with message:

`
User "system:node:ip-10-0-243-205.us-east-2.compute.internal" cannot get resource "volumeattachments" in API group "storage.k8s.io" at the cluster scope: no relationship found between node 'ip-10-0-243-205.us-east-2.compute.internal' and this object
`

See steps to reproduce below, it's quite a complex condition. It happens when a pod is restarted, a CSI driver "busy" (i.e. times out) + KCM restarted at a wrong time.

### What did you expect to happen?

Pods start just fine.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?


1. Create a Pod that uses an attachable CSI volume.
2. Delete the Pod. Make sure it unmounts successfully, but any `ControllerUnpublish` fails with a transient error, such as timeout. The external attacher continues to detach the volume at this point.
3. Stop kube-controller-manager (KCM) and start a new one. Wait for any leader election etc - it's important for the new KCM to populate A/D controller with no pod using the detaching volume. Let the A/D controller to observe detach error.
4. Create a new Pod on the same node that uses the same volume.
5. Let the CSI driver to detach the volume (i.e. stop injecting any transient errors).

At this point:

- The external attacher succeeds detaching the volume, VolumeAttachment is deleted.
- The volume is marked as attached in node status (!!!) despite no VolumeAttachment exists. A/D controller does not even try to create a new VolumeAttachment, the volume is marked as attached in its Actual State of World (ASW).
- Kubelet tries to mount the volume, but WaitForAttach fails with: `cannot get resource "volumeattachments" in API group "storage.k8s.io" at the cluster scope: no relationship found between node '127.0.0.1' and this object`, basically forever.

title: Kubernetes Docker Config Json Globbing Not As Documented
body:
### What happened?
K8s Docker config json globbing is not as documented for subdomain wildcarding.
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/credentialprovider/keyring.go

### Impact
The user impact is that people create `imagePullSecrets` and corresponding configuration to use private registries and the credentials do not get used leading to `4xx` with the registry, image pull errors and some confusion. 

### What did you expect to happen?

Docs indicate that host glob `*my-registry.io` would work to be used as auth for e.g
```
foo.my-registry.io
foo.bar.my-registry.io
```
* https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/images/#config-json
* https://github.com/kubernetes/website/blob/main/content/en/docs/concepts/containers/images.md

Run package unit tests with the following cases added to `TestURLsMatch`:

title: Can't restrict access from K8s nodes with loadBalancerSourceRanges for proxy-mode=ipvs
body:
### What happened?

When using loadBalancerSourceRanges to allow access only from CIDRs outside the cluster segment, access from the K8s nodes (or pods with hostNetwork:true) should be rejected, but for proxy-mode=ipvs it works.

/sig network
/area kube-proxy
/area ipvs

### What did you expect to happen?

Access from K8s nodes should be rejected in the same way as for proxy-mode=iptables

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Define a service with loadBalancerSourceRanges that allows access from a cidr outside the cluster, e.g.

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: alpine
spec:
  loadBalancerSourceRanges:
#  - "192.168.1.0/24"
  - "192.168.2.0/24"
#  - "fd00::c0a8:100/120"
  - "fd00::c0a8:200/120"
  ipFamilyPolicy: RequireDualStack
  selector:
    app: alpine
  type: LoadBalancer
  allocateLoadBalancerNodePorts: false
  ports:
  - port: 5001
    name: nc
```
The K8s nodes have addresses on 192.168.1.0/24 and fd00::c0a8:100/120.

Make sure a loadBalancerIP is assigned (in this example 10.0.0.0/32) and try to access it from a K8s node:
```
# With proxy.mode=ipvs
> nc 10.0.0.0:5001
alpine-f6c8bd7db-zljnl    # (works)
# With proxy.mode=iptables
# nc 10.0.0.0:5001
# (hangs...)
```

### Anything else we need to know?

Same for both ipv4 and ipv6.

This is related to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119524 since a fix requires that the `nodeID` passed to the `kube-proxy` is correct. Please see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119524#issuecomment-1655389139

title: [ValidatingAdmissionPolicy] Param authorization checked only at compile time
body:
### What happened?

There is a check to ensure that the param provided to `ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding` is capable of being read by the user who created the admission policy when it is first validated:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a88defe09a13dac704ce27d1072292a99e152cee/pkg/registry/admissionregistration/validatingadmissionpolicybinding/authz.go#L88-L108

This check is never performed again. At runtime, the controller makes use of a the loopback Kubernetes client to fetch params, possibly giving access to protected resources to CEL expressions:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a88defe09a13dac704ce27d1072292a99e152cee/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/validatingadmissionpolicy/controller.go#L303-L307

### What did you expect to happen?

I have a open questions about the security of this:

1. Is it sufficient for the only creator of the `Binding` to have access to the params to make use of it in CEL expressions defined by the `Policy`?
2. Should this check be performed every time params are used, to guard against changing permissions

title: Performance analysis of x-kubernetes-validations
body:
As soon as possible, and certainly before the [CEL validation rules for CRDs feature](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-api-machinery/2876-crd-validation-expression-language/README.md) reaches GA, we need to understand its performance implications to CR create/update.

- Baseline CRD that has a trivial OpenAPIv3 schema
- CRD with complex OpenAPIv3 schema, but no CEL rules
- CRD with simple CEL rules
- CRD with lost of cheap CEL rules (high compilation cost and CEL program memory utilization)
- CRD with CEL rules near the estimated cost limit
- CRD with webhook that performs the same task as a CRD with CEL rules

We also need good benchmarks should prevent performance regressions.

It would also be good to look at existing issues that impact performance AND scale: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/109099.  Does CEL make these much worse?

[KCCM]: service controller predicates might impact ingress SLO on GCP with InstanceGroup based Load Balancing
body:
### What happened?

In 1.26 the service controller in the Kubernetes cloud controller manage (KCCM) introduced a new mechanism for syncing load balancers based on predicates. The predicates applied will depend on "service classes", specifically if it's `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` or `Cluster`, see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.26/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L944-L947

This implementation is not well suited for internal GCP load balancers which use InstanceGroups. @People from Google, feel free to correct me: any cluster has all nodes grouped together into an instance group. Service of `type: LoadBalancer` have individual GCP load balancers, but these load balancers end up referencing the same instance group (which is the cluster's instance group). This means that the inclusion/exclusion predicates for any service, will trickle down and impact the cluster's global instance group, thereby impacting other services which don't necessarily apply the same set of predicates. Ex: `externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster` services exclude `NotReady` nodes, whereas `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` do not. A Node going `NotReady` will therefore be removed from all backends for `externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster` services, however on GCP with load balancer solution based on InstanceGroups: this means that the same node will be removed from all backends for `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` services too.    

This is NOT a problem on >= 1.27 using the feature `StableLoadBalancerNodeSet`, because all services on 1.27 using that feature gate will have the same set of predicates. 

### What did you expect to happen?

Node updates requiring the removal of the instance from load balancers belonging to services of `externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster` should not impact other services of `externalTrafficPolicy: Local`.

Bring up a cluster using "Internal load bala

title: kube-proxy SNAT policy for nodeport should only be performed on traffic originating from the pod on the current host
body:
### What happened?

Pod A runs on host node-1, where there are multiple network cards (eth0:10.10.11.1, eth1:192.168.10.11). Pod A is associated with service A, which is a nodeport type and provides a nodeport 30001; Pod B runs on host node-2, and accesses Pod A through 192.168.10.11:30001. At this time, the source IP obtained inside Pod A is the IP of eth0 on node-1, and the expected IP is eth1.

### What did you expect to happen?


The source IP should be displayed as the IP of the network card through which the traffic actually passes. Some gateway applications require the setting of an x-forwarded for request header, which may be used in security policies. When multiple network cards exist, it is necessary to set the x-forwarded for to the correct business network card IP address.


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

create nginx pod and config x-forward-for header，access nginx using pod host ip and service nodeport。

### Anything else we need to know?

kube-proxy add this rule for nodeport traffic:
-A KUBE-POSTROUTING -m comment --comment "kubernetes service traffic requiring SNAT" -j MASQUERADE

MASQUERADE rule will change the source ip to the network card with the highest priority on the host.

title: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy: variable expression type not recognized as return type in expression that evaluates the variable
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Variables field is added to ValidatingAdmissionPolicy in 1.28. Currently the usage of variables would expect a operator associated. 
e.g. (thanks to Mariam Fahmy for raising the issue)
```
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
metadata:
  name: "chech-deployment-labels"
spec:
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups:   ["apps"]
      apiVersions: ["v1"]
      operations:  ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
      resources:   ["deployments"]
  variables:
    - name: environment
      expression: "has(object.metadata.labels) && 'env' in object.metadata.labels && object.metadata.labels['env'] == 'prod'"
  validations:
    - expression: "variables.environment"
      message: "Deployment labels must be env=prod"
```
Above will fail with error: 
```
The ValidatingAdmissionPolicy "chech-deployment-labels" is invalid: spec.validations[0].expression: Invalid value: "variables.environment": must evaluate to bool
```
Meanwhile the `- expression: "variables.environment == true"` will pass.

The reason is when variables be evaluated to non dyn type(like bool or string), it will require special handling(like casting) since we use dyn type everywhere. 

### Why is this needed?

It might confuse user.

title: CRI getFsInfo logs errors for valid filesystems mounted after kubelet start
body:
**What happened**:

New overlay filesystems created for Pods after kubelet start trigger repeated error messages. For example:

```
cri_stats_provider.go:375] Failed to get the info of the filesystem with mountpoint "/var/lib/containers/storage/overlay/2243263dc8ba6c55d8867d3e47bcaaa145d15f0ace19420824d639d86defe2e3/merged": failed to get device for dir "/var/lib/containers/storage/overlay/2243263dc8ba6c55d8867d3e47bcaaa145d15f0ace19420824d639d86defe2e3/merged": could not find device with major: 0, minor: 83 in cached partitions map.
```

Error messages are logged every 10 seconds for every filesystem created after kubelet start. For large kubelet nodes, this issue creates an excessive amount of error logs.

**What you expected to happen**:

New overlay filesystems created for Pods after kubelet start should not log error messages.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Use cri_stats_provider with cri-o and configure overlay storage. UsingLegacyCadvisorStats() needs to return false per https://github.com/cri-o/cri-o/pull/3054 for cri_stats_provider to be used. Start with an empty /var/lib/containers/storage and schedule Pods on the node.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

As part of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/59475, cadvisor.GetFsInfoByFsUUID() was changed to cadvisor.GetDirFsInfo() in getFsInfo(); however, the test for cadvisorfs.ErrNoSuchDevice was not modified, changing how getFsInfo() handles a cache miss from cadvisor. 

cadvisor caches UUIDs/partitions/mounts on kubelet start and the cache is never refreshed. Given that it's expected that getFsInfo() will fail to retrieve data from cadvisor (see comments in ImageFsStats() and https://github.com/kubernetes/heapster/issues/1793), this condition should not be logged as an error. Alternatively, cadvisor fs could be modified to refresh on cache miss enabling getFsInfo() to return data on these filesystems.

title: Provide a multiplication method for the resource.Quantity
body:
### What would you like to be added?

I'd like to add a multiplication method for the resource.Quantity.


### Why is this needed?

Currently, the resource package provides helper methods to calculate Quantity, such as `Add` and `Sub`:

- https://github.com/kubernetes/apimachinery/blob/8d1258da8f386b809d312cdda316366d5612f54e/pkg/api/resource/quantity.go#L565-L567
- https://github.com/kubernetes/apimachinery/blob/8d1258da8f386b809d312cdda316366d5612f54e/pkg/api/resource/quantity.go#L582-L584

Batch workloads often replicate the same PodTemplate, and controllers calculate the resources needed for all containers.

In that case, It is inconvenient to call the `Add` function as many times as podTemplate, so I would like to create a helper function for multiplication.
