title: kubelet applies defaults to Pods and causes could not process manifest file
body:
### What happened?

When I put a Pod yaml file without `metadata.name` in `/etc/kubernetes/manifests`, started the kubelet and hoped it would create the corresponding staticPod for me, I got the following error, which also caused the staticPod to not be created.

```
Jul 06 22:46:02 cloud kubelet[2930835]: E0706 22:46:02.905289 2930835 file.go:187] "Could not process manifest file" err="invalid pod: [metadata.name: Invalid value: \"-cloud\": a lowercase RFC 1123 subdomain must consist of lower case alphanumeric characters, '-' or '.', and must start and end with an alphanumeric character (e.g. 'example.com', regex used for validation is '[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*')]" path="/etc/kubernetes/manifests/yurthub.yaml"
```

I then read the kubelet code and quickly found the problem. When kubelet tries to decode the pod yaml file, it will apply default values and validate the pod. The function to apply the defaults is in `pkg/kubelet/config/common.go L56`.

In this function, the `metadata.name` is set.

```go
pod.Name = generatePodName(pod.Name, nodeName)

// Generate a pod name that is unique among nodes by appending the nodeName.
func generatePodName(name string, nodeName types.NodeName) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s", name, strings.ToLower(string(nodeName)))
}
```

This causes an error when `metadata.name` is not set, because it causes the '-' character to be at the front.

I think kubelet should circumvent this error, because `metadata.name` is optional, It is possible for this field not to be set.

### What did you expect to happen?

When Pod's `metadata.name` is not set, the '-' character at the start should be avoided, as it will cause an error.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Prepare a Pod yaml file without `metadata.name` and set it into `/etc/kubernetes/manifests`.

title: Re work pkg/util/ipset.Validate()
CEL estimated cost treats enums as strings of unbounded length
body:
### What happened?

@robscott pointed out to me that a CEL x-kubernetes-validations rule in a CRD was hitting the estimated cost limit when performing a simple "string has prefix" check on an en enum field.

Putting a `maxLength` limit in the OpenAPI of the enum string field fixed the problem, but having to add a limit like this is counter-intuitive and unnecessary, since the allowed enum values already make the max allowed length obvious.

### What did you expect to happen?

The apiserver automatically computes the max length of an enum as the length of the longest allowed enum value. 

I believe we already refuse evaluate CEL rules on values that fail OpenAPI value validation, since we rely in the value validations to establish all length limits.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

I haven't tested it locally, but something like this should work (given enough nested arrays):

```
openAPIV3Schema:
  type: object
  properties:
    spec:
      type: array
      items:
        type: array
        nested:
          type: string
          enum: ["low", "medium", "high"]
          x-kubernetes-validations:
            - rule: 'self.matches("Prefix")'
```

### Anything else we need to know?

As a workaround, one can manually set `maxLength` on the string enum, e.g.:

```
          type: string
          maxLength: 6
          enum: ["low", "medium", "high"]
          x-kubernetes-validations:
            - rule: 'self.matches("Prefix")'
```

title: [KCCM]: handle coalesced node updates in the service controller
body:
### What happened?

On big clusters with a lot of churn, Node updates can be frequent. The service controller in the Kubernetes cloud controller manager (KCCM) uses an edge-triggered resource watcher for what concerns handling the Update events, see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L160-L176

This means that Node events which should trigger a sync (ex: the addition/removal of the label `exclude-from-load-balancer`) can be missed if multiple updates occur on the same object in a short amount of time. 

The `UpdateFunc` doc bloc even explicitly warns about patterns such as the one described above, see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/controller.go#L207-L212

This pattern has always been used in the KCCM, but I believe that since some Node conditions which used to trigger re-syncs have been removed since 1.26, the error can be triggered more often now. Specifically on < 1.26, the `NotReady` condition on the Node used to trigger a re-sync. This condition usually occurs when the Node stabilizes, sometime after its initial creation. This covered the existing issue.    

/sig network
/sig cloud-provider
/cc @aojea @thockin 


### What did you expect to happen?

All Node events should get enqueued. The Node controller will compare the current set of nodes in its informer cache to the last set of Nodes it synced, if a change is observed the load balancer is synced, see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L746-L751 - this shouldn't even lead to additional syncs because of this.

title: [Code-generator] `--extra-peer-dirs` flag  is not supported by new `kube-codegen.sh` script
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Earlier it was possible to pass `--extra-peer-dirs` flag to `conversion-gen` while calling `generate-internal-groups.sh` script. 
Now with the new `kube-codegen.sh` script, `conversion-gen` is called under `kube::codegen::gen_helpers` which doesnot support any other flags apart from `--input-pkg-root`, `--output-base` and `--boilerplate`.

As it can be seen here there is no option to pass flag to conversion-gen
```
 "${gobin}/conversion-gen" \
            -v "${v}" \
            -O zz_generated.conversion \
            --go-header-file "${boilerplate}" \
            --output-base "${out_base}" \
            "${inputs[@]}"
```
https://github.com/kubernetes/code-generator/blob/e4611069dfb4b0c04c7751afae1b9fef64828964/kube_codegen.sh#L203-L208

Earlier in the `generate-internal-groups.sh`  script, it was considering all the inputs passed
```
  echo "Generating conversions"
  "${gobin}/conversion-gen" \
      --input-dirs "$(codegen::join , "${ALL_FQ_APIS[@]}")" \
      -O zz_generated.conversion \
      "$@"
```

### Why is this needed?

`--extra-peer-dirs` flag is supported by `conversion-gen` under the hood, but the `kube::codegen::gen_helpers` function in `kube-codegen.sh` script is not allowing the flag.

title: Containers with "m" used as abbreviation in memory limits fail to start on Linux, and consume 1e+9 too much memory on Windows
body:
## Background

https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-compute-resources-container/

  Limits and requests for memory are measured in bytes. You can express memory as a plain integer or as a fixed-point integer using one of these suffixes: E, P, T, G, M, K. You can also use the power-of-two equivalents: Ei, Pi, Ti, Gi, Mi, Ki. For example, the following represent roughly the same value:

  `128974848, 129e6, 129M, 123Mi`

## Bug

If someone uses a lowercase letter, for example `m`, that has inconsistent behavior between Windows & Linux. `m` is a valid suffix for CPU but not memory.

> Note: `docker` command line options do support `m`, `b`, `k` and `g`. [docker resource constraints](https://docs.docker.com/config/containers/resource_constraints/#limit-a-containers-access-to-memory)

On Linux, the `m` prefix is dropped if it's included as part of a memory resource. This resource allocation will create an allocation of 300 bytes, not 300 Megabytes or Mebibytes. That's too small and container startup will fail. See [full error logs](#full-error-logs) below.

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: nginx-test1
spec:
  containers:
  - name: nginx
    image: library/nginx
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: 1
        memory: 800m
    ports:
      - containerPort: 80
  nodeSelector:
    "beta.kubernetes.io/os": linux
```



On Windows, the `m` prefix is treated the same as `M`. This resource allocation will be 300 Megabytes, and container startup will succeed.

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: iis-test2
spec:
  containers:
  - name: iis
    image: mcr.microsoft.com/windows/servercore/iis:windowsservercore-ltsc2019
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: 1
        memory: 800m
    ports:
      - containerPort: 80
  nodeSelector:
    "beta.kubernetes.io/os": windows
```

This would have the same effect on resources as `docker run --memory 800m -d mcr.microsoft.com/window

title: pod_status_manager_state: checkpoint is corrupted
body:
### What happened?

After enabling In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling, if deploy a pod without setting memory (or cpu) request, kubelet will be failed at its second restart


### What did you expect to happen?

kubelet restart successfully

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. start kubelet with In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling enabled
2. deploy a pod without setting memory request, e.g: 
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - image: nginx:1.24.0
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    name: nginx
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 100m
```
3. restart kubelet for the first time
4. restart kubelet for the second time
5. kubelet will fail with error: `panic: could not restore state from checkpoint: checkpoint is corrupted, please drain this node and delete pod allocation checkpoint file "/var/lib/kubelet/pod_status_manager_state" before restarting Kubelet` 

### Anything else we need to know?

After deploying the pod, the following information is saved in the file `pod_status_manager_state`:

```
      "nginx": {
        "cpu": "100m"
      }
```
Then restart kubelet for the first time, the relevant content in the file becomes: 
```
      "nginx": {
        "cpu": "100m",
        "memory": "0"
      }
```
------
When deploying the pod, as there are no records in the checkpoint (`pod_status_manager_state`), kubelet will get resource config from `pod.Spec.Container.Resources`  directly and save it to the checkpoint (without memory request)
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3125009dd1ebdde499a810110ba1f6d3fb05698f/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L2504-L2521
When restarting kubelet for the first time, it will restore the previously saved data from the checkpoint. Since the memory request was not previously set, it will be set to an empty value and resaved to the checkpoint
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3125009dd1ebdde499a810110ba1f6d3fb05698

### What happened?

Running containers in privileged mode is not recommended as privileged containers run with all [linux capabilities](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/capabilities.7.html) enabled and can access the host's resources. Running containers in privileged mode opens number of security threads such as breakout to underlying host OS.

Currently the kube-proxy DaemonSet runs in privileged mode.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/863a462eeccca4c24bf4c4e9012f5ebccade70a2/cluster/addons/kube-proxy/kube-proxy-ds.yaml#L50-L51

https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/kubelet-in-userns/#configuring-kube-proxy describes how to run kube-proxy in "rootless". To my understanding "rootless" != non-privileged mode but this configuration can be also used for running in non-privileged mode. However I see that following issues with it:
1. In the provided kube-proxy component config in https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/kubelet-in-userns/#configuring-kube-proxy we have to disable certain settins to prevent kube-proxy from ensuring sysctls (which is allowed only in privileged container).

And I don't see a way how to disable kube-proxy from ensuring this sysctl from its component config.

title: scheduler: register default EventsToRegister in only some extension points
body:
## What

register default EventsToRegister only for PreFilter, Filter, Reserve, and Permit plugins.

Currently, we register default EventsToRegister for all plugins that don't have EnqueueExtension.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2c6c4566eff972d6c1320b5f8ad795f88c822d09/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L551-L554

## Why

EventsToRegister affects which events the scheduler watches, and when registered events come, the scheduling queue requeue Pods according to them. The queue checks the event can make Pod schedulable or not via QueueingHint from pInfo.UnschedulablePlugins.
Given this fact, plugins that never be registered in pInfo.UnschedulablePlugins don't need to have EventsToRegister. 
And, currently, only PreFilter, Filter, Reserve, and Permit affect pInfo.UnschedulablePlugins. Meaning all other plugins' EventsToRegister actually don't affect anything, and to register default EventsToRegister to other plugins could result in watching events in vain, which all of PreFilter, Filter, Reserve, and Permit plugins aren't interested in.

/kind feature
/sig scheduling

I utilize two customized metrics, A and B, in my HPA system. A is a gauge-based metric called SLA Metric, while B is a count-based metric that tracks failed requests with HTTP status code 502 or 503 from Istio. These metrics are scraped by Prometheus.

To use custom metrics in HPA, we're employing Kube Metrics Adapter [link](https://github.com/zalando-incubator/kube-metrics-adapter). When the application load increases, the value of the SLA Metric also increases, and then the pods scale up until they reach the maximum replica count as expected.
However, the problem arises when the load dissipates, and the pods never scale down. Despite the SLA Metric's value being below the target in Prometheus, the HPA description still displays the metric value with a stale value that can be above or below the target.

One possible reason for this is that Metric B, which relies on Istio requests, shows up as unknown since there have been no failed requests with the 502 or 503 status codes. Thus, the Prometheus query fails.
We have noticed this behavior after upgrading Kube from version 1.21 to 1.24 and changing the HPA version from autoscaling/v2beta2 to autoscaling/v2.

title: High cpu usage in json.compact call
body:
### What happened?

I was debugging performance of case with heavy watch traffic of CRD objects and found interesting suboptimality: we burn significant amount of CPU on json.compact calls that deserialize JSONs to validate correctness of already serialized objects: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2559168/169510517-e5b23c43-b15c-4f6d-adf1-cf36ccf6e203.png)

It looks like while in WatchServer.ServeHTTP we manage to reuse serialized objects (cachingObject) in object serialization: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7af5a7bfc51d0455d8b2322ae9e72ed66fb1b8f9/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/watch.go#L247-L251, we then wrap this objects in metav1.Event object and serialize it again: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7af5a7bfc51d0455d8b2322ae9e72ed66fb1b8f9/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/watch.go#L271

While that object consists of single enum and already serialized raw object it is expected that its serialization will be cheap. And it is for protobufs where we simply copy bytes:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7af5a7bfc51d0455d8b2322ae9e72ed66fb1b8f9/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/runtime/generated.pb.go#L187-L192

But for json, it's much more expensive:
* We return already serialized object if re.Raw is set (it is on watch code path): https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7af5a7bfc51d0455d8b2322ae9e72ed66fb1b8f9/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/runtime/extension.go#L37-L51
* but golang's json serializer compacts that json to check its validity: https://github.com/golang/go/blob/d8762b2f4532cc2e5ec539670b88bbc469a13938/src/encoding/json/encode.go#L498

This validation happens in each watcher separately contributing to significant CPU usage.

### What did you expect to happen?

We won't deserialize/compact objects in each watch client separately.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Open watch for objects using j

For a dualstack Service, its endpoints are only from one IP family.

	if len(svc.Spec.IPFamilies) > 0 {

```

2 single-family endpoints per backend pod: Make no change to the [Kubernetes Endpoints API](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.10/#endpoints-v1-core). Treat each IPv4/IPv6 address as separate, distinct endpoints, and include each address in the comma-separated list of addresses in an 'Endpoints' API object.

Given a phased approach, the 2 single-family endpoint approach represents the least disruptive change. Services will select only the endpoints that match the spec.ipFamily defined in the Service.

title: node.status.nodeInfo.kubeProxyVersion is a lie
body:
`v1.Node` has a field `.status.nodeInfo.kubeProxyVersion`, about which [the API docs](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.0/staging/src/k8s.io/api/core/v1/types.go#L5250) say:

```
// KubeProxy Version reported by the node.
KubeProxyVersion string `json:"kubeProxyVersion" protobuf:"bytes,8,opt,name=kubeProxyVersion"`
```

but the field is [set by kubelet](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.0/pkg/kubelet/nodestatus/setters.go#L401), which does not actually know the kube-proxy version:

```
node.Status.NodeInfo.KubeletVersion = version.Get().String()
// TODO: kube-proxy might be different version from kubelet in the future
node.Status.NodeInfo.KubeProxyVersion = version.Get().String()
```

Not only is it possible that the kube-proxy version is different from the kubelet version, it's also possible that kube-proxy isn't even running on the machine.

This field should be marked as deprecated. Ideally kubelet would stop setting it but that might be considered an API break? If kubelet is going to continue setting it, then the API docs and the kubelet source should both be updated to indicate that the field is just an alias for `kubeletVersion` and does not actually indicate the kube-proxy version, and will be set even if kube-proxy is not running.

(Noticed by @liggitt)

/sig node
/sig network

A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where a user that can create pods on Windows nodes may be able to escalate to admin privileges on those nodes. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if they include Windows nodes.

### Am I vulnerable?

Any kubernetes environment with Windows nodes is impacted.  Run `kubectl get nodes -l kubernetes.io/os=windows` to see if any Windows nodes are in use.

#### Affected Versions

- kubelet <= v1.28.0
- kubelet <= v1.27.4
- kubelet <= v1.26.7
- kubelet <= v1.25.12
- kubelet <= v1.24.16

### How do I mitigate this vulnerability?

The provided patch fully mitigates the vulnerability and has no known side effects.  Full mitigation for this class of issues requires patches applied for CVE-2023-3676, CVE-2023-3955, and CVE-2023-3893.

Outside of applying the provided patch, there are no known mitigations to this vulnerability.

#### Fixed Versions

- kubelet master - fixed by #120127
- kubelet v1.28.1 - fixed by #120129
- kubelet v1.27.5 - fixed by #120130
- kubelet v1.26.8 - fixed by #120131
- kubelet v1.25.13 - fixed by #120132
- kubelet v1.24.17 - fixed by #120133

To upgrade, refer to the documentation:
https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/cluster-upgrade/

### Detection

Kubernetes audit logs can be used to detect if this vulnerability is being exploited. Pod create events with embedded powershell commands are a strong indication of exploitation. Config maps and secrets that contain embedded powershell commands and are mounted into pods are also a strong indication of exploitation.

If you find evidence that this vulnerability has been exploited, please contact security@kubernetes.io

This vulnerability was reported by Tomer Peled @tomerpeled92

The issue was fixed and coordinated

title: Excessive etcd list+watch operations on 1.27+
body:
### What happened?

*moving the discussion from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/115918#issuecomment-1789808263*

One of our users has put together a synthetic test that seems to break the RepicaSet controller when using Kine, and I'm trying to track that down
1. Create 100 pods in a namepace, each with a unique label
2. In that same namespace, create 50 pods that each watch pods in that namespace, with a labelSelector that matches the unique label on one of the pods. Each of the 50 "observers" should see events from a single "observed" pod.

On 1.26 and prior, each of the 50 observers shared the cluster-wide etcd watch, with the apiserver providing filtering.

With this change, etcd logs show that each watch now kicks off a new pair of list+watch operations against etcd, which must then be filtered by the apiserver to apply the selectors. This is a significant increase in overhead against the datastore, and requires more work of the apiserver; I think operators should have been made aware of this change so that they could update capacity planning accordingly.

Here are interleaved logs from the apiserver (with --v=4) and etcd (with -log-level=debug --logger=zap) showing  1:1 correlation between apiserver watches and etcd range requests. Unfortunately it doesn't appear that I can get logs showing the watch that follows the range, but from tracing in kine I can confirm that this also occurs.

title: How to access app  in k8s cluster by aggregator apiservice with Authorization header
body:
I deployed a third-party web application in the k8s cluster with deployment+service. The web application mainly provides login verification api  and other web service api. After calling the login api, Bearer token will be responsed, and be set into Authorization Bearer token before calling other web service api. It works well when requests are from k8s cluster inside.


This k8s cluster has a public IP, but strict firewall rules and security group rules are set up. Only port 6443 is exposed to the public network, and additional ports are not allowed. I am wondering if there is any way to access the web app in the cluster through the public IP+6443 port of the k8s cluster.


I found the k8s aggregator apiservice. After creating the apiservice and pointing it to my web service,  running  `curl -X POST --cacert ./ca.crt --cert ./client.crt --key . /client.key -H "contentType: application/json" -d '{username: xx, password: yy}' https://ip:6443/api/v1/namespaces/default/services/my-svc:port-80/proxy/api/login` is success, and the Bearer token is responsed, but I run (`curl -X POST --cacert ./ca.crt - -cert ./client.crt --key ./client.key -H "contentType: application/json" -H '{Authorization: Bearer xxx}' https://ip:6443/api/v1/namespaces/default/services/my-svc:port-80/proxy/api/other-api`) to request other api, it returns 401 Unauthorized . I suspect that the header in request was intercepted or consumed by kube-apiserver, and was not passed to my web app.

Here is my question: 1. Is there any other way to access the applications in the cluster through the public IP + 6443 port of the k8s cluster? 2. How can I access the applications in the cluster without changing the firewall and security group rules or the third-party application source code, just using the Authorization Bearer toker header through kube-apiserver to complete the authentication?

body:
### What happened?

Kubernetes e2e suite: [It] [sig-api-machinery] Garbage collector should support orphan deletion of custom resources [sig-api-machinery]

As stated in https://github.com/kubernetes/apimachinery/blob/master/pkg/util/wait/poll.go#L84:
```
// Deprecated: This method does not return errors from context, use PollUntilContextTimeout.
// Note that the new method will no longer return ErrWaitTimeout and instead return errors
// defined by the context package. Will be removed in a future release.
func PollWithContext(ctx context.Context, interval, timeout time.Duration, condition ConditionWithContextFunc) error {
	return poll(ctx, false, poller(interval, timeout), condition)
}
```
When I replace PollWithContext with PollUntilContextTimeout in the test directory, the CI always returns the following error:
[Related links](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/121401/pull-kubernetes-e2e-ec2/1717584584415121408)

In [It] at: test/e2e/apimachinery/garbage_collector.go:1110 @ 10/26/23 17:14:08.526
}
```

### What did you expect to happen?

A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where a user that can create pods on Windows nodes running kubernetes-csi-proxy may be able to escalate to admin privileges on those nodes. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if they include Windows nodes running kubernetes-csi-proxy.

### Am I vulnerable?

Any kubernetes environment with Windows nodes that are running kubernetes-csi-proxy is impacted.  This is a common default configuration on Windows nodes.  Run `kubectl get nodes -l kubernetes.io/os=windows` to see if any Windows nodes are in use.

#### Affected Versions

- kubernetes-csi-proxy <= v2.0.0-alpha.0
- kubernetes-csi-proxy <= v1.1.2

### How do I mitigate this vulnerability?

The provided patch fully mitigates the vulnerability and has no known side effects.  Full mitigation for this class of issues requires patches applied for CVE-2023-3676, CVE-2023-3955, and CVE-2023-3893.

Outside of applying the provided patch, there are no known mitigations to this vulnerability.

#### Fixed Versions

- kubernetes-csi-proxy master - fixed by https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/csi-proxy/pull/306
- kubernetes-csi-proxy v2.0.0-alpha.1 - fixed by https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/csi-proxy/pull/307
- kubernetes-csi-proxy v1.1.3 - fixed by https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/csi-proxy/pull/306

To upgrade: cordon the node, stop the associated Windows service, replace the csi-proxy.exe binary, restart the associated Windows service, and un-cordon the node.  See the installation docs for more details: https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/csi-proxy#installation

title: introduce QueueingHint for wise-enqueueing
body:
### What would you like to be added?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/87850 tries to almost remove the flushing unschedulable Pods into activeQ.
Then, after that, almost all moving to activeQ can be associated with certain events.

Here, I'd propose two changes for PreEnqueue so that we can utilize PreEnqueue for wise-enqueueing.

#### 1. adding parameters about what happens to `PreEnqueue`.

- `event`: By which event the pod will be moved back to schedQ/backoffQ. It's represented by [`framework.ClusterEvent`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/27344212cec3538a44b166db721b083e8865c32e/pkg/scheduler/framework/types.go#L77).
- `involvedObj`: the object involved in that event.
  - For example, the given event is "Node deleted", the involvedObj will be that deleted Node.

```go
type EnqueuePlugin interface {
    Plugin
    PreEnqueue(ctx context.Context, state *CycleState, p *v1.Pod, event framework.ClusterEvent, involvedObj runtime.Object) *Status
}
```

Also, in the following cases, `event` and `involvedObj` would be empty:
  - If an enqueued Pod is a newly created.
  - If the Pod will be backed to schedQ/backoffQ by flushing.

#### 2. return `Skip` if the plugin does nothing with that event.

e.g., `NodeAffinity` returns `Success` when a Node gets labels that match with Pod's NodeSelector. But, it returns `Skip` when a Node gets labels that doesn't match with Pod's NodeSelector.

Currently, `PreEnqueue`'s return status is quite simple: 
- all PreEnqueue plugins return Success -> enqueue to activeQ.
- any PreEnqueue plugin return non-Success -> don't enqueue to activeQ.

By introducing `Skip`, we can change here like:
- all PreEnqueue plugins which are in [UnschedulablePlugins](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/27344212cec3538a44b166db721b083e8865c32e/pkg/scheduler/framework/types.go#L104) return Skip -> don't enqueue to activeQ.

### What would you like to be added?

The ipvs scheduler is configured by clusters, can we allow it to be configured by service?

For our situation is we configure the `rr` for the cluster, all the node will pick the first the same apiserver since server list is well sorted, so when we create a daemonset with all newly started apiserver, the daemonset will direct to the first apiserver which will cause a lot load to it and cause it OOM cuz the list request is quite expensive. Allowed configure IPVS scheduler per service

title: Kube-Proxy IPVS mode support port hash and fallback in sh schedule
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Current `sh` load balancing policy only performs hashing of sourcing IP, the server load maybe really high when only a single client is sending bunch of data to the server; So like this MR, we definitely need source port hash flag in `sh` policy as well

Another things is the `sh` don't have the fallback flag enabled, which the client will have no endpoints to send when the hashed one is unready and the weight set to zero. Can refer to this [patch](https://lore.kernel.org/lkml/20130619095425.GA20145@eldamar.org.uk/)

### Why is this needed?

kubeproxy IPVS mod should include src-port hash and fallback flag in  `sh` policy.

title: When Pod fails to schedule during bind stage, PVC and PV are still bound, prevent pod reschedule to another node
body:
### What happened?

In my cluster, I have three nodes, each belonging to different availability zones: us-east-1a, us-east-1b, and us-east-1c. I have a StatefulSet resource with a replica count of 3, set podManagementPolicy as Parallel to allow creating pods in parallel. The StatefulSet resource uses volumeClaimTemplate to declare the use of persistent storage. To ensure that the three pods are scheduled in different zones, I've also configured the topologySpreadConstraints.

When kube-scheduler decides to schedule pod-A to node-1(assume pod in kube-scheduler's cache), kube-scheduler will add an annotation `volume.kubernetes.io/selected-node: node-1` on PVC to notify external provisioner to create PV and bound with PVC for pod-A.

The problem is sometimes pod-A scheduling fails at bind stage for some reason. kube-scheduler removes the assumed pod-A from cache, and adds it to the backoff queue for rescheduling, **but PV and PVC for pod-A remain bound to the node and won't be cleaned up.**

The next pod, pod-B, is then scheduled and happens to be assigned to the same node, without considering that the previous pod-A had already created a PVC and PV on that node. Pod-B successfully schedules on node-1. 

**When it's time to reschedule pod-A, it's unable to schedule to another node because pod-A's PVC is already bound to node-1. Furthermore, due to topologySpreadConstraints limits, pod-A cannot be scheduled to the same node (node-1) as pod-B**. As a result, pod-A remains in pending state forever. Even if I add new nodes to the cluster later, pod-A still won't be scheduled to other nodes. Currently, the only solution is to delete pod-A and PVC-A so that pod-A can be rescheduled to a different node.

Here is the StatefulSet definition.
```yaml
 kubectl get statefulsets elastic-master -o yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: "2023-10-23T06:33:35Z"
  generation: 2
  labels:
    app: elasticsearch
    role: master
  na

title: Image pull from private registry fails because of missing credentials
body:
### What happened?

When trying to pull a image from a private registry the request is executed without any kind of authorization.

The secret is manually created with
`kubectl create secret generic regcred --from-file=.dockerconfigjson=dc.json --type=kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson`

`dc.json` is a file like the following:
```json
{
    "auths": {
        "somecontainerregistry.azurecr.io": {
            "auth": "XYZ"
        }
    }
}
```
where XYZ is the base64 encoding of `:refresh_token` (there is no username as I want to dynamically get a token from a OAuth endpoint)

My pod is then specifying the `imagePullSecret` pointing to the `regcred` from above.

When creating the pod, after setting up a mitmproxy, I can see the following requests:
- HEAD to `https://somecontainerregistry.azurecr.io/v2/whateverimage/manifests/latest` which correctly fails with a 401 and returns a `Www-Authenticate` header set to `Bearer realm="https://somecontainerregistry.azurecr.io/oauth2/token",service="somecontainerregistry.azurecr.io",scope="repository:whateverimage:pull"`
- Then the request to the `/oauth2/token` endpoint is executed. The problem here is that it is executed as a GET (opposed to being a POST) and without the expected URLEncoded form including the refresh_token from the imagePullSecret.

Executing a `HTTPS_PROXY="127.0.0.1:8080" crictl pull --auth "XYZ"  somecontainerregistry.azurecr.io/whateverimage` gives me no issues and the image is pulled successfully.

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected the kubelet and the container runtime to properly talk to each other, but I am either doing something wrong or there is a bug 😄

- Create an Azure Container Registry (or any image registry that is capable of OAuth AuthN)

title: [KCCM]: service update while node sync is processing might impact ingress
body:
### What happened?

The Kubernetes cloud controller manager uses resource watchers to sync load balancers, a Node/Service watcher. The Node watcher is slower by nature since any Node event will sync all service load balancers on the cluster. The service watcher is quicker since it only syncs the service load balancer which the event relates to. 

How slow a Node sync is will vary on the cluster, i.e: amount of Services of `type: LoadBalancer` and Nodes, but on big clusters with a lot of churn: the time to process one Node sync can be sufficiently slow to have the cache of Nodes go stale w.r.t the actual cluster state. The cache of Nodes is here the resource informer cache. When syncing Nodes the Node control loop will list all Nodes in its cache and then iterate over all Services and sync their load balancers in parallel, see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L799-L818

If any Service experiences an update needing a load balancer sync, the Service controller will also list the Nodes in the informer cache, but retrieve a more up-to-date copy, see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L438-L451. 

During upgrades or similar operations where a lot of Nodes get added/deleted: it's rather easy for the following to occur;

1. Node sync is processing, N load balancers are synced
2. NodeY is added
2. Service update triggers sync for load balancer X. It lists and adds NodeY to the load balancer set
3. Node sync processes load balancer Y and removes NodeY from the load balancer set 

This add + remove from the load balancer set might impact ingress SLOs for any application running on NodeY after its creation. 

/sig network
/cc @thockin @aojea

Any node added to the load balancer set which doesn't have a reason (i.e: [predicate](https://github.com/kuberne

title: DNS-1035 validation mismatch
body:
### What happened?

When creating a `Service` with a name that starts with a digit, Kubernetes return this error:

 
> Service "94924f13c1c1d259-d98b37350debffcf" is invalid: metadata.name: Invalid value: "94924f13c1c1d259-d98b37350debffcf": a DNS-1035 label must consist of lower case alphanumeric characters or '-', start with an alphabetic character, and end with an alphanumeric character (e.g. 'my-name',  or 'abc-123', regex used for validation is '\[a-z\]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?')


### What did you expect to happen?

I would expect that you could create a `Service` with a name that starts with a digit, as the error states:

```
a DNS-1035 label [...] start with an alphabetic character, and end with an alphanumeric character
```

But the regex shown in the message doesn't match the error description:
```
 '[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?')
```
should be
```
 '[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?')
```

Apply this resource to k8s

```yaml
apiVersion: v1

  name: 001-service

  selector:

title: Define new well-known annotation: `kubernetes.io/display-name`
body:
### What would you like to be added?

~~We~~ VMware would like to define a new, well-known annotation, `kubernetes.io/display-name`, per [_Well-known labels, annotations, and taints_](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/labels-annotations-taints). A quick tl;dr about the history of this issue is as follows:

* There is a PR open at https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/43658.
* This topic has been discussed in [this thread](https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C5P3FE08M/p1697837862269049) in the `#sig-architecture` channel from k8s Slack.
* @sftim has been a giant help in shepherding this issue.
* @dims requested this issue be filed and assigned to `#sig-cli`.

/sig cli

### Why is this needed?

To my knowledge, such an annotation does not exist, and while [`kubernetes.io/description`](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/labels-annotations-taints/#description) is close, it is not exactly the same thing. ~~We~~ VMware was likely to introduce a similar annotation internally due to the lack of a standard, well-known annotation for this use case in upstream K8s. However, after speaking with some folks, we opted to [engage](https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C1J0BPD2M/p1697816976615399) `#sig-docs`, who suggested we [reach out](https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C5P3FE08M/p1697837862269049) to `#sig-architecture` about adding this annotation to upstream K8.

#### Goals

1. **Standard approach for mutable, human-readable name on K8s objects**
  Users & non-interactive processes should be able to read/write a K8s object's human-readable name.

1. **Well-defined syntax and character set for human-readable names**
  Users & non-interactive processes should be able to read/write human-readable names using UTF-16.

1. **Support for human-readable name in standard human-readable column**
  Applications that surface or present K8s objects should be able to refer to a common location for surfacing an object's human-readable name.

title: Resource(CPU, memory, device, topology) managers don't consider restartable init containers
body:
### What happened?

Resource(CPU, memory, topology) managers don't consider restartable init containers.

- [ ] CPU manager: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119447
- [ ] Memory manager: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120715
- [ ] Device manager: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120461
- [ ] Topology manager:

---

When cpu-manager-policy is static and you create a guaranteed pod with a restartable init container,
a restartable init container shares its static CPUs with a regular container.


### What did you expect to happen?

A restartable init container should not share its CPU requirement with the regular containers.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```
$ cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f - 
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  initContainers:
  - name: init-1
    image: ubuntu
    command:
    - sh
    - -c
    - |
      grep Cpus_allowed_list /proc/self/status | cut -f2
    volumeMounts:
    - name: shared
      mountPath: /tmp/shared
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: 8
        memory: 100Mi
  - name: restartable-init-2
    image: ubuntu
    command:
    - sh
    - -c
    - |
      grep Cpus_allowed_list /proc/self/status | cut -f2
      sleep 300s
    volumeMounts:
    - name: shared
      mountPath: /tmp/shared
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: 4
        memory: 200Mi
    restartPolicy: Always
  containers:
  - name: regular-3
    image: ubuntu
    command:
    - sh
    - -c
    - |
      grep Cpus_allowed_list /proc/self/status | cut -f2
      sleep 300s
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: 4
        memory: 300Mi
    volumeMounts:
    - name: shared
      mountPath: /tmp/shared
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 1
  volumes:
  - name: shared
    emptyDir: {}
  restartPolicy: Never
EOF

title: CVE-2023-5528: Insufficient input sanitization in in-tree storage plugin leads to privilege escalation on Windows nodes
body:
CVSS Rating: [CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H) - **HIGH** (7.2)

A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where a user that can create pods and persistent volumes on Windows nodes may be able to escalate to admin privileges on those nodes. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if they are using an in-tree storage plugin for Windows nodes.

### Am I vulnerable?

Any kubernetes environment with Windows nodes is impacted.  Run `kubectl get nodes -l kubernetes.io/os=windows` to see if any Windows nodes are in use.

#### Affected Versions

- kubelet >= v1.8.0 (including all later minor versions)

### How do I mitigate this vulnerability?

The provided patch fully mitigates the vulnerability.

Outside of applying the provided patch, there are no known mitigations to this vulnerability.

#### Fixed Versions

- kubelet master - fixed by #121881
- kubelet v1.28.4 - fixed by #121882
- kubelet v1.27.8 - fixed by #121883
- kubelet v1.26.11 - fixed by #121884
- kubelet v1.25.16 - fixed by #121885

To upgrade, refer to the documentation:
https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/cluster-management/#upgrading-a-cluster

### Detection

Kubernetes audit logs can be used to detect if this vulnerability is being exploited. Persistent Volume create events with local path fields containing special characters are a strong indication of exploitation.

If you find evidence that this vulnerability has been exploited, please contact security@kubernetes.io

#### Acknowledgements

This vulnerability was reported by Tomer Peled [@tomerpeled92](https://github.com/tomerpeled92)

The issue was fixed and coordinated by the fix team:

Mark Rossetti @marosset

title: Need a way for user to specify container labels
body:
I need a way for a client creating a pod to put something in the pod that specifies some container labels.  Please note that I am **_not_** talking about making a pod's containers inherit all the pod's labels.  Rather, I am talking about a new bit of specification for labels that are intended just for the containers.

For my use case, it suffices to give the client a way to specify one set of labels, and that set gets put on every container of the pod.  I could also use a more flexible interface that gives independent control over the labels going on to each container.

To be concrete, the less expressive interface would be an additional pod spec field whose name is something like `containerLabels` and whose value is a map from label name to label value.  The more expressive interface would be an additional container spec field like that, but named something simpler like `labels`.

For prototyping the less expressive interface, we might start with supporting annotations of the form `alpha.kubernetes.io/containers-labels/XXX=YYY`, each meaning to put the label `XXX=YYY` on each container of the pod.

The more expressive interface could be prototyped with something like annotations of the form `alpha.kubernetes.io/container-labels/ZZZ/XXX=YYY`, each meaning that the label `XXX=YYY` is to be put on the pod's container named `ZZZ`.

title: About the future of existing PV generated from the in-tree format yaml once the CSI migration is complete
body:
### What would you like to be added?

As the title mentions, our customers are concerned about the future of existing PV generated from the in-tree format yaml once the CSI migration is complete.
I am stuck on this and would really like to know what the SIG storage policy is on this matter.

### Why is this needed?

CSI Migration allows PVs with Specs in in-tree format to be manipulated via CSI, but PVs with Specs in CSI format are treated differently from in-trees,
our customers is concerned about whether In-tree Spec and PVs generated from In-tree format yaml files will work forever in the future, or whether we need to convert from PVs generated from In-tree format yaml files to CSI PVs once the CSI migration is complete, and do we have to recreate the deployment via CSI spec if the in-tree format yaml file is no longer available.

I believe some translate functions that translate In-tree PV Spec into the CSI PV format have been added in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/83098 ,
could I ask that when will these functions be maintained ?
Will it be maintained forever and not deleted in the future? And is it okay if I assume that existing In-tree PVs will continue to be used in the future?  (Specs will remain as In-tree PVs and will not need to be modified, but will be converted by translate functions and will always be processed by CSI plugins forever in the future).

I would like to know what is the policy of SIG storage. Thank you very much.

/sig storage

title: Access `negotiation.MediaTypeOptions` from `rest.Lister` implementation
body:
### What would you like to be added?

We would like to the ability to access `negotiation.MediaTypeOptions` from within `rest.Lister` implementations.

### Why is this needed?

I am working on a project at Grafana that implements [rest.Lister](https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apiserver@v0.28.2/pkg/registry/rest#Lister) with Grafana's existing SQL backed storage. We are currently using [rest.TableConvertor](https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apiserver@v0.28.2/pkg/registry/rest#TableConvertor) to format the response, but we would like to optimize the SQL query when the user requests the `Table` response format.

For example:
```
kubectl get dashboards
NAME                                   TITLE       CREATED AT
d08ca90a-64c8-459e-b2fc-69d30cb5e01e   example     2023-11-17T19:22:47Z
```

Right now the query would look like:

```sql
SELECT * from dashboard;
```

But if we knew it was a request for the `Table` format, it could be limited to:

```sql
SELECT uid, title, created from dashboard;
```

*Note: In this example `uid` from the dashboard query is used as the K8s object's `metadata.name`.*

It appears that [negotiation.NegotiateOutputMediaType](https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apiserver@v0.28.2/pkg/endpoints/handlers/negotiation#NegotiateOutputMediaType) is what is normally used to determine this, but it’s unclear what to use for the `EndpointRestrictions` argument when implementing `List`. It seems like [handlers.RequestScope](https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers#RequestScope) is used for `EndpointRestrictions` in the apiserver code, but `handlers.RequestScope` is not accessible from within our `rest.Lister` implementation.

title: CVE feed title doesn't mention project
body:
### What happened?

Our feed, when rendered, doesn't say which project / product it's for.

Example (from my workplace):
> Auto-refreshing Official CVE Feed [CVE-2023-2878](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/118419)
> secrets-store-csi-driver discloses service account tokens in logs 
>
> A security issue was discovered in secrets-store-csi-driver where an actor with access to the driver logs could observe service account tokens. These tokens could then potentially be exchanged with… (86 KiB)

There's no mention that this is a Kubernetes component.

Now, _I_ know it's a Kubernetes component, but it's not going to be obvious to everyone.

### What did you expect to happen?

Entries in the feed show up with context that mentions Kubernetes.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Subscribe to the official CVE feed

### Anything else we need to know?

/sig security

Lots of feed renderers will pick up that there's a Kubernetes issue tracker URL in the item, but we can't rely on that.

I would title the feed “Kubernetes vulnerability announcements”.

title: Add a new podLogsDirectory setting to Kubelet
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Add a new podLogsDirectory setting to Kubelet, which will provide users with ability to set `podLogsRootDirectory`.

### Why is this needed?

The text below is copied from original [issue](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/108384):

The root directory for pod logs is /var/log/pods as default, and doesn't support modification.
Sometimes we want container logs to be output to a specified place according to the disk usage plan.

Actually, docker outputs container logs to its workspace, and then creates symlink to /var/log/pods (dockershim does). That's ok.
After runtime switchs to others, like containerd, we should provide a way to set podLogsRootDirectory.

title: Pod phase changed when container exits with 0 in 1.27
body:
/sig node

After https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/115331 the phase of terminal pods killed with killPodFunc is determined based on the exit codes of the containers. This was discovered in the context of preemption while doing a cherry-pick to 1.26, and observing that the phase changed: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118221.

Summary of the phase transitions when the pod container exits with 0 (when restartPolicy=Always):
| scenario                                         | 1.26             |  1.27 
| -----------                                          | -----------       |  -----------
|  preemption                                  |  Failed         | Succeeded
|  eviction due to node pressure                      |  Failed         | Succeeded
| node shutdown                            | Failed | Succeeded
| active deadline exceeded           | Failed          | Failed

Note that eviction due to exceeding storage limits isn't affected because it uses grace period=0. In that case, SIGKILL is sent directly, and the containers end with 137. 

Are the changed phases a bug?
- if a bug, how to approach fixing it?
- if not a bug, we should clean up the setting of the phase as Failed in the component status updates, like here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/preemption/preemption.go#L106

Note: The change of phase for "node shutdown" was discovered earlier and uncovered a DaemonSet issue that was fixed: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/117018

title: NCC-E003660-PA6: Additive Access Controls
body:
### NCC-E003660-PA6: Additive Access Controls
This issue was reported in the [Kubernetes 1.24 Security Audit Report](https://github.com/kubernetes/sig-security/blob/main/sig-security-external-audit/security-audit-2021-2022/findings/Kubernetes%20v1.24%20Final%20Report.pdf)

**Description**
In Kubernetes, authorization is handled at the API level based on the authorization modes
the API server is configured with. The main user-facing Kubernetes authorization mode,
`RBAC`, provides a role-based access control (RBAC) system that maps principals to
operations related to resources across single namespaces or entire clusters based on
whether the Roles and/or RoleBindings are Cluster-level. However, the Kubernetes RBAC
model does not support Deny rules, instead only identifying whether a user has a
permission to access a given resource in a given way. Due to this, the model can be
considered to “fail open” in the event that a principal is, through generic or over-broad role
definitions, granted unintended permissions. 

The Kubernetes’ authorization model is structured such that it will sequentially try all configured authorization modes until one returns an explicit `DecisionAllow` or `DecisionDeny`, or return an error in the event that they all return `DecisionNoOpinion`. [Link to reference](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.24.3/plugin/pkg/auth/authorizer/rbac/rbac.go#L126). While this model can be used similarly to
Kubernetes’ admission controller model, in which an allowed Boolean is used and for
which any failed validation will result in an overall error, in practice, internal authorizers
such as Node and RBAC can only return DecisionNoOpinion on failure, not DecisionDeny ,
preventing them from fully rejecting accesses.

**Recommendation**
Consider enhancing the current RBAC authorization mode or introducing a new RBAC mode
with support for explicit Deny rules that return `DecisionDeny`.

title: Env variable is missing in container, after cleanup of duplications in deployment
body:
### What happened?

Unintentionally we defined the same env twice in our deployment.
```
          env:
          - name: PARAMETER
            value: "example"
          - name: PARAMETER
            value: "example"
```
The deployment itself has worked and the env in container was available.
Later, we cleaned it up - simply removed the duplicated entry
```
          env:
          - name: PARAMETER
            value: "example"
```
After deployment, the application broke, because the env was not available in the affected container.
After we deployed it again, the variable was set again

### What did you expect to happen?

After the cleanup, the env variable must still be set in the container because it is still defined in the deployment.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

title: service-account-token falsely reported as created when there is not service-account
body:
### What happened?

While creating the secret with `type: kubernetes.io/service-account-token` it is reported as created:

```
$ kubectl  apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: my-secret
  annotations:
    kubernetes.io/service-account.name: my-sa
type: kubernetes.io/service-account-token
EOF

> secret/my-secret created
```

but it is actually not created until there is a corresponding service-account existing:

```
$ kubectl get sa my-sa
Error from server (NotFound): serviceaccounts "my-sa" not found

$ kubectl get secrets --all-namespaces
No resources found
```

> On the recreation (`kubectl apply`) of the secret it is once again reported as `created`

### What did you expect to happen?

The secret should not be reported as created, or there should be a warning that it won't be visible until the `service-account` exists/

On the recreation (running `kubectl apply` again ) of the secret it is once again reported as `created` instead of expected `unchanged`/`updated`

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

execute:

```
kubectl  apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: my-secret
  annotations:
    kubernetes.io/service-account.name: not-existing-service-account
type: kubernetes.io/service-account-token
EOF

secret/my-secret created

title: Make specific fields inside CSIDriver.Spec mutable
body:
### What would you like to be added?

This is being proposed as change from https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/2119

From` discussion among sig-storage, we agreed to make following fields inside `CSIDriver` mutable:

* FSGroupPolicy: it’s safe to be mutable
If two pods use the same volume, one of them can see it if fsGroup, the other without it. Seems to be OK.

* PodInfoOnMount: it’s safe to be mutable but Drivers must handle that



### Why is this needed?

We decided to do this, so as to support mutability of aforementioned fields as properly supported operation, rather than forcing users to delete and recreate `CSIDriver` object.

title: Mount point may become local without calling `NodePublishVolume` after node rebooting
body:
### What happened?

This issue is very similar to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/117513, they have the same symptom: remote volumes of the pods are becoming local mount point after rebooting the Node. And this issue is triggered by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/117513.

The difference is that in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/117513, kubelet didn't call `NodeStageVolume`, so the global mount point is local, but it will still call `NodePublishVolume` for the pod to bind mount the pod volume to the global mount point. Whereas in this issue, kubelet neither call `NodeStageVolume` globally nor call `NodePublishVolume` for the pod. 

This is more harmful: After writing some data to the pod volume, pod can't be deleted because kubelet encounter `directory not empty` error while unmounting the pod volume:
 
![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/44308864/b1cc4e04-15ac-4730-a862-54eddf2a4960)


Reproduce steps:
1. Create a cluster with one Node
2. Create a deployment with **two replicas**(say `pod-1` and `pod-2`) using Non-attachable volume (for example Azurefile)
3. Shutdown the Node
4. Delete `pod-1` with option `--force` (Use force deletion to simulate the situation that mount point was left over before rebooting the Node.)
5. Bring back the Node
6. `pod-2` is always in Running state, however, after rebooting, it won't call `NodePublishVolume` and the volume it uses is local volume.

### What did you expect to happen?

`pod-2` should call `NodePublishVolume`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

As mentioned above.

_No response_

title: verify-typecheck checks binaries that don't actually get built
body:
In #118017 I tried to reorganize the kube-proxy build a bit, and ran into the problem that verify-typecheck failed because `cmd/kube-proxy` was no longer buildable on darwin/amd64 and darwin/arm64. This was surprising because we don't build kube-proxy on OS X.

It seems like verify-typecheck ought to be taking `KUBE_SUPPORTED_*_PLATFORMS` / `KUBE_*_TARGETS` from `hack/lib/golang.sh` into account when deciding what to check. There's no reason to be checking the OS X type compatibility of binaries that we don't build on OS X.

title: Request timeout not respected while listing from storage
body:
### What happened?

It is possible to issue a list request which exceeds the duration set by the request-timeout apiserver flag. The request-timeout flag does not appear to be enforced when the apiserver is decoding the response from etcd. 

Specifically, listing a large number of CRDs from etcd can result in high request latency from using json encoding compared to protobuf encoding. While overall etcd latency is low, the overall listing from storage latency may be over the 1 minute timeout, particularly if the apiserver needs to fetch multiple pages from etcd.



### What did you expect to happen?

We expected the list requests to be subject to the duration specified by the request-timeout flag when this latency is coming from the listing from storage phase of the request.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create 4000 CRs and list all the objects from etcd in 2 pages of 2000 objects. If the time to list 1 page + decode takes around 50s, listing 2 pages will result in the listing from storage phase of the request taking  around 1 minute and 40s before the request fails and the client is returned a 500 response code.

title: No proper scheduling retries could be made when Extender filters out some Nodes
body:
### What happened?

When Extender filters out some Nodes, we don't set any unschedulable plugins at all. It means Extender is completely ignored during the requeueing process.

So, what's happening is:
- If Extender filters out all Nodes during scheduling, this Pod is soon retried because this Pod doesn't have any plugin name in unschedulable plugins.
- If Extender filters out some Nodes during scheduling and plugins filter out all other Nodes, this Pod is retried based on plugins' QueueingHint. Even if any cluster events happen and it could change Extender's decision (but not any plugins' decision), this Pod won't be requeued to activeQ/backoffQ.

The latter case is serious because it could make Pods being stuck in unschedulable pod pool in 5min.

### What did you expect to happen?

We should have a short-term solution for the latter case. 
We can requeue Pods, which were rejected by Extender, by any kind of cluster events because we cannot know which events make Pods schedulable.

Eventually, this issue makes us wonder how Pods rejected by Extender should be requeued. We cannot implement QHint equivalent in Extenders because it'd be too slow to call Extender every time any cluster events happen. Probably, somehow implementing EventsToRegister equivalent in Extender? 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Use Extender which does something in Filter.

title: Scheduler's default plugin returns an invalid score that is not in the range of [0, 100], resulting in no Pods being scheduled
body:
### What happened?

Scheduler's default plugin returns an invalid score that is not in the range of [0, 100], resulting in no Pods being scheduled:
```
E1127 19:48:13.221979   66549 schedule_one.go:130] "Error selecting node for pod" err="applying score defaultWeights on Score plugins: plugin \"PodTopologySpread\" returns an invalid score 300, it should in the range of [0, 100] after normalizing" pod="default/test-multi-point-xxxxxxxx"
```

After investigation, I found that there was a bug in the code that built the framework when the scheduler started. When using the plugins declared in the regular extension point to override the plugins declared in the MultiPoint, the traversed variable `enabledSet` will be modified in the following loop:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ad9b60e2c9ddb21e8b00cabbe27e639638a0ea88/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L523-L534

This may cause **a same scoring plugin** (e.g. `PodTopologySpread`) **to be loaded multiple times**:
```
f.scorePlugins: []framework.ScorePlugin{(*noderesources.Fit)(0xc000922e10), (*podtopologyspread.PodTopologySpread)(0xc0000ab100), (*podtopologyspread.PodTopologySpread)(0xc0000ab100), (*tainttoleration.TaintToleration)(0xc0003f3690), (*nodeaffinity.NodeAffinity)(0xc0003997a0), (*volumebinding.VolumeBinding)(0xc0003db7a0), (*interpodaffinity.InterPodAffinity)(0xc00038f3b0), (*noderesources.BalancedAllocation)(0xc000063680), (*imagelocality.ImageLocality)(0xc000b45320)}

title: Deletion of upgrade-health-check during the upgrade preflight could fail  due to a race condition and surfaced as CreateJob failure
body:
### What happened?

I have seen false positives in the upgrade preflight where `CreateJob` fails because `kube-system/upgrade-health-check` job is not found when trying to delete it.

Looking at the code, there is a bit of inconsistent treatment in the creation and the deletion of the job during the cluster health check.

When creating the job to test if a job can be created on the cluster, [the job creation accounts for a possibility of race condition and have a retry to mitigate this](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cmd/kubeadm/app/phases/upgrade/health.go#L154-L163).

However, the deletion code doesn't take care of the same race condition in two places:
1. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cmd/kubeadm/app/phases/upgrade/health.go#L142-L147
2. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cmd/kubeadm/app/phases/upgrade/health.go#L149-L152

Specifically, I think [deleteHealthCheckJob](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cmd/kubeadm/app/phases/upgrade/health.go#L197-L204) should ignore `NotFound` errors to be resilient to the cases where the job was deleted by another client (basically `--ignore-not-found=true` is what we want here).


### What did you expect to happen?

Ignore `NotFound` error when attempting to delete the `upgrade-health-check` job.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

With 3 control plane node setup and run `kubeadm upgrade plan` on three nodes at the same time and this probably happens once in a while.

### Anything else we need to know?

If the requested change sounds reasonable, I can work on making the changes.

### What happened?

A pod uses a PVC with volumeMode: Block. The block volume is backed by a block device on the node (which is created by some CSI storage providers). title: sched framework: expose NodeInfo in all functions of PluginsRunner interface
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Scheduler framework exposes a series of functions in PluginsRunner interface for out-of-tree plugins to implement custom functionalities:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6f8d38406a7f16fc9cc9b72789a9b826105b1b54/pkg/scheduler/framework/interface.go#L601-L605

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6f8d38406a7f16fc9cc9b72789a9b826105b1b54/pkg/scheduler/framework/interface.go#L725-L750

However, `RunPreScorePlugins` and `RunScorePlugins` exposes `Node` instead of `NodeInfo` like other functions. It causes inconvenient UX for plugin users like [koordinator](https://github.com/koordinator-sh/koordinator). For example, one of the requirements is to find an optimal preemption candidate node in PostFilter plugins. `NodeInfo` carries important extra info during the preemption dryrun, and w/o consuming `NodeInfo`, running `Run{Pre}ScorePlugins` would be non-sense. To work around it, users have to plumb very specific and sometime ugly semantics themselves which should have been avoided.

### Why is this needed?

- consistent function signature - all use NodeInfo
- unleash more potential to use scheduler framework natively w/o hacks

title: endpoints not configured with MinimizeIPTablesRestore
body:
### What happened?

To test out the MinimizeIPTablesRestore feature enabled in 1.27 by default we enabled the setting in 1.26 and discovered that it appears to not configure endpoints properly everytime.
While the version in 1.26 is still alpha I have not found any significant changes, bug reports or backports in the changelog regarding this.

It seems sometimes kube-proxy does not see that the endpoints of a service need to be updated despite the api endpointslice having changed. This typically is not that visible with externalTrafficPolicy Cluster services as some other endpoint still is configured, but in the case of low replica services or externalTrafficPolicy Local services this can lead to service disruption due to the only endpoint on the local node not getting configured while other components see the update correctly and direct traffic there.


For example this two pod deployment both pods ready since hours:

title: Scheduler evaluates many nodes even if there are no scoring plugins defined
body:
### What happened?

Even when no scoring plugins are defined, scheduler always attempts to find multiple nodes where the pod can run. This is unnecessary (and therefore inefficient) when we know ahead of time that there will be no difference between how those nodes are scored. 

### What did you expect to happen?

If we're going to pick a random node, we can just as well cut short the search after finding the first match.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Configure scheduler without any scoring plugins and see that mulitple nodes are evaluated anyway.

title: noderesourcefit: change PodUpdate QHint to take a new scenario into consideration
body:
See: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122234#issuecomment-1859021909
/kind feature
/sig scheduling
/assign @carlory 

---

After https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122234, the scheduler starts to use QueueingHint registered for Pod/Updated event to determine whether unschedulable Pods update make them schedulable. 
We have to change PodUpdate QHint in noderesourcefit to take into consideration that the pod might equal the unscheduled pod.
i.e.,
```go
func (f *Fit) isSchedulableAfterPodChange(logger klog.Logger, pod *v1.Pod, oldObj, newObj interface{}) (framework.QueueingHint, error) {
  // maybe pod == newObj (oldObj)
}
```

title: NodeAffinity/NodeUnschedulable QueueingHint may miss Node related events that make Pod schedulable
body:
### What happened?

/kind bug
/triage accepted
/priority urgent
/sig scheduling
/assign

NodeAffinity QueueingHint may miss Node related events that make Pod schedulable because of preCheck.
It's similar to: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119177#issuecomment-1820091877

So:
1. Node is added. But, it's filtered out by preCheck (due to node's unready or whatever) and the scheduling queue doesn't receive NodeAdded. (noderesourcefit cannot receive NodeAdded.)
2. Node is updated and ready now. But, this event is NodeUpdated.

In such scenarios, NodeAffinity may return `QueueSkip` to the event due to (2).
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/nodeaffinity/node_affinity.go#L94-L131

### What did you expect to happen?

We have to loosen the filtering in `isSchedulableAfterNodeChange` until preCheck is removed.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/110175

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a Pod with NodeAffinity under the situation where no Node can accommodate the Pod.
2. Create a new Node.

It may cause the above problematic scenario.

title: No proper scheduling retries could be made when Extender filters out some Nodes
body:
### What happened?

When Extender filters out some Nodes, we don't set any unschedulable plugins at all. It means Extender is completely ignored during the requeueing process.

So, what's happening is:
- If Extender filters out all Nodes during scheduling, this Pod is soon retried because this Pod doesn't have any plugin name in unschedulable plugins.
- If Extender filters out some Nodes during scheduling and plugins filter out all other Nodes, this Pod is retried based on plugins' QueueingHint. Even if any cluster events happen and it could change Extender's decision (but not any plugins' decision), this Pod won't be requeued to activeQ/backoffQ.

The latter case is serious because it could make Pods being stuck in unschedulable pod pool in 5min.

### What did you expect to happen?

We should have a short-term solution for the latter case. 
We can requeue Pods, which were rejected by Extender, by any kind of cluster events because we cannot know which events make Pods schedulable.

Eventually, this issue makes us wonder how Pods rejected by Extender should be requeued. We cannot implement QHint equivalent in Extenders because it'd be too slow to call Extender every time any cluster events happen. Probably, somehow implementing EventsToRegister equivalent in Extender? 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Use Extender which does something in Filter.

body:
### What would you like to be added?

[This patch PR](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118036/files) was applied earlier this year to k8s >=1.28. As a vulnerability that shows up in the Federal compliance scans/reports that are binding to enterprises operating in the Federal space, it should be included in security patches of all supported k8s release lines, including 1.26 and 1.27. Without that, we are put in the position of having to rush out major releases with breaking changes to attain a security patch. 

The CVE in question is https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-2253
It was resolved in https://github.com/distribution/distribution/releases/tag/v2.8.2. And the PR above bumps kubernetes to use v2.8.2, so I think all the work is done; it just needs a backport.

Resolves https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-2253

title: [Discussion]`InPlacePodVerticalScaling` may lead to assumed pod with rotten state
body:
### What happened?

With `InPlacePodVerticalScaling` enabled, an assumed pod might be scaled down with its resources, however, we'll return directly here
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4111bef430515f6e76213c4be84c0dd1e9722e20/pkg/scheduler/eventhandlers.go#L145-L147


This may lead to the pod cache with rotten state, and moreover, some unschedulable pods which failed by nodeResourceFit might be re-schedulable but now it's unworkable.

However, I think **the intermediate state is acceptable**, it's short and after pod is binded, we'll receive a new pod updated event which will **refresh the cache**, also re-trigger the rescheduling processes, finally **reach the eventual consistence**.

Then what we should do here is  adding more explanations.

title: QueueingHints(Pod/delete) have to consider that "unassume Pod" is treated as Pod/delete
body:
### What happened?


> Side question: What if the unscheduled Pod was assumed?
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122360#discussion_r1431547953

This question made me wonder what if the Pod was unassumed. 

1. Only one Node which can accomodate only one Pod exists. 
2. Pod-a is assumed to the Node. (but not yet actually bound)
3. Pod-b is rejected because the scheduler assumes Pod-a.
4. Pod-a is somehow unassumed. **It's treated as Pod/delete event.**
5. Pod-a goes to the scheduling queue. Now, the Node has a free space though, will Pod-b be retried? Well, it's depending on the implementation of QHints of Pod/delete...

---

These are plugins that have this problem.

- [ ] nodeports
- [ ] noderesource

For example, nodeports:

> // If the deleted pod is unscheduled, it doesn't make the target pod schedulable.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/42ab3b7b40c34e91b63589ae905ed918752a4a36/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/nodeports/node_ports.go#L136

This is not true, because if the deleted pod is assumed Pod, it makes the target pod schedulable.


### What did you expect to happen?

1. Only one Node which can accomodate only one Pod exists. 
2. Pod-a is assumed to the Node. (but not yet actually bound)
3. Pod-b is rejected because the scheduler assumes Pod-a.
4. Pod-a is somehow unassumed. **It's treated as Pod/delete event.**
5. Pod-a goes to the scheduling queue. **noderesourcefit receives Pod/delete event by (4), and it moves Pod-b to activeQ/backoffQ.**


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

The above scenario.

title: Already API-evicted Pods do not get evicted by the kubelet eviction manager (memory pressure, ephemeral storage pressure)
body:
### What happened?

When pods have a long _terminationGracePeriod_ and get evicted by downscaling or some other reason (via API) the eviction is initiated which respects that long _terminationGracePeriod_. This works fine.

If the pods need to be evicted due to memory pressure on the node after the already initiated API eviction there is no more eviction done with the specified _evictionMaxPodGracePeriod_ of the kubelet. This means that the second eviction due to e.g. memory pressure cannot be successful at all when you have large _terminationGracePeriod_ on your pod and there was a prior unrelated API eviction.

![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/28532557/9d83248f-7dfe-49b0-88b0-7b7e9f73faf6)


### What did you expect to happen?

The eviction manager triggered eviction due to memory pressure should still be issued with the specified _evictionMaxPodGracePeriod_ even if there was a prior API based eviction with a large terminationGracePeriod.



### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- Create a workload pod that does ignore sig-terms
- Specify a large _terminationGracePeriod_ for that pod, do not set any memory limits for the pod
- Specify a small _evictionMaxPodGracePeriod_ for the kubelet on the node
- API evict the Pod
- Make sure the kubelet wants to evict the pod (e.g. by allocating memory inside pod until the node is under memory pressure)


### Anything else we need to know?

The bug was not present in k8s 1.25.x

title: Add "action" property to NetworkPolicySpec
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Add an `action` property to NetworkPolicySpec, which is an enum described as such:

* `accept` - Accept the packet
* `drop` - Drop the packet, allowing for a timeout on the other side
* `reject` - Immediately send back an error packet (such as a TCP RST)

For `iptables`, this would closely match the ACCEPT, DROP, REJECT actions, respectively.

This property could be expanded to include other actions, such as `log`, if they are compatible with the underlying sub-systems, either in the new feature, or future feature requests.

### Why is this needed?

The existing [NetworkPolicySpec](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.28/#networkpolicyspec-v1-networking-k8s-io) has an implied action here described here:

> Outgoing traffic is allowed if there are no NetworkPolicies selecting the pod (and cluster policy otherwise allows the traffic), OR if the traffic matches at least one egress rule across all of the NetworkPolicy objects whose podSelector matches the pod. If this field is empty then this NetworkPolicy limits all outgoing traffic (and serves solely to ensure that the pods it selects are isolated by default).

So, the action taken for a given network policy is not explicitly declared, and could change depending on if the rules are removed or added.

This implied action is confusing, prone to error, and can lead to security mistakes.  Most firewall software, whether it's Layer 4 devices or Layer 7 WAFs, has some sort of explicit action field to communicate exactly what will happen if it matches a rule or ruleset.

Furthermore, there is no option to reject packets, which can be a more useful troubleshooting step, as it does not require waiting for timeouts from the client side, and has a more specific error message.
